{{ill|September 18|ja|9月18日}} (Autumn Festival) }} '''Unakorowake Shrine''' (宇奈己呂和気神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Kōriyama|ja|郡山市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai shrine|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}}), and its former shrine ranking under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. [[Unakoro Waki Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''{{ill|Seoritsuhime|ja|瀬織津比売命}}''' - One of the {{ill|Haraedo-no-Ōkami|ja|祓戸大神}} '''Secondary deity''' * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡神}}: Hondawake-no-Mikoto ({{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇}}) == History == === Founding === According to ancient records, during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Kōnin|ja|光仁天皇}}, disturbances caused by the {{ill|Emishi|ja|蝦夷}} were widespread in the Mutsu Province. In the first year of {{ill|Ten'ō|ja|天応}} ({{ill|781|ja|781年}}), the court dispatched {{ill|Fujiwara no Oguro|ja|藤原小黒麿}} as inspector of Mutsu and Dewa, but he failed to suppress the unrest. The following year, in the first year of {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦}} ({{ill|782|ja|782年}}), the newly enthroned {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇}} sent {{ill|Ōtomo no Yakamochi|ja|大伴家持}} to the region as an inspector and commander. After seeking divine guidance on {{ill|Takahatayama|ja|高旗山}}, Yakamochi established a shrine to enshrine Seoritsuhime, whose divine power reportedly aided in subduing the unrest. Later, in the 3rd year of Enryaku ({{ill|784|ja|784年}}), the shrine was moved from Takahatayama to its current location in Yamazaki. At that time, {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡大神}} (Hondawake-no-Mikoto) was enshrined as a secondary deity. A stone shrine (okumiya) remains on the summit of Takahatayama, and an information board at the mountain trailhead near {{ill|Genda Onsen|ja|源田温泉}} recounts this history. According to shrine records, the shrine’s origins trace back to the 11th year of Emperor Kinmei ({{ill|550|ja|550年}}?). During that time, Seoritsuhime was believed to have manifested on Takahatayama's summit. Seoritsuhime, identified as a deity born from the purification of {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊耶那岐命}} at Awagihara, was venerated for her ability to cleanse impurities and pacify disturbances. === Historical Overview === As recorded in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}, the shrine was granted the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 14th year of {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} ({{ill|847|ja|847年}}). According to the {{ill|Ruijū Kokushi|ja|類聚国史}}, the shrine's rank was elevated to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 11th year of {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} ({{ill|869|ja|869年}}). In {{ill|927|ja|927年}}, the shrine was listed as a {{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} and became the main shrine of the three {{ill|Shikinai shrines|ja|式内社}} in the Asaka District, receiving deep veneration from both rulers and local residents. It was also designated the total shrine (sōsha) for the {{ill|33 communities of Asaka|ja|安積三十三郷}}. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, {{ill|Kudō Suketsune|ja|工藤祐経}}, appointed as local governor, introduced deities from the {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋大社}} and other shrines in Izu Province as subordinate shrines. The shrine was further restored by local rulers such as {{ill|Ashina clan|ja|蘆名氏}} and {{ill|Gamo Ujisato|ja|蒲生氏郷}}, and it received land grants and other support. === typeings === * {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} 14 ({{ill|847|ja|847年}}): Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}) * {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} 11 ({{ill|869|ja|869年}}): Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}) == Shrine Grounds == === Main Shrine === The shrine comprises a haiden, heiden, and a covered three-bay honden in {{ill|Miya-zukuri|ja|流造}} style. The honden features three doors, symbolizing the deities enshrined. Presently, the shrine honors two deities, with one seat left vacant. {{ill|September 18|ja|9月18日}} (Autumn Festival) }} '''Unakorowake Shrine''' (宇奈己呂和気神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Kōriyama|ja|郡山市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai shrine|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}}), and its former shrine ranking under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. [[Unakoro Waki Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''{{ill|Seoritsuhime|ja|瀬織津比売命}}''' - One of the {{ill|Haraedo-no-Ōkami|ja|祓戸大神}} '''Secondary deity''' * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡神}}: Hondawake-no-Mikoto ({{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇}}) == History == === Founding === According to ancient records, during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Kōnin|ja|光仁天皇}}, disturbances caused by the {{ill|Emishi|ja|蝦夷}} were widespread in the Mutsu Province. In the first year of {{ill|Ten'ō|ja|天応}} ({{ill|781|ja|781年}}), the court dispatched {{ill|Fujiwara no Oguro|ja|藤原小黒麿}} as inspector of Mutsu and Dewa, but he failed to suppress the unrest. The following year, in the first year of {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦}} ({{ill|782|ja|782年}}), the newly enthroned {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇}} sent {{ill|Ōtomo no Yakamochi|ja|大伴家持}} to the region as an inspector and commander. After seeking divine guidance on {{ill|Takahatayama|ja|高旗山}}, Yakamochi established a shrine to enshrine Seoritsuhime, whose divine power reportedly aided in subduing the unrest. Later, in the 3rd year of Enryaku ({{ill|784|ja|784年}}), the shrine was moved from Takahatayama to its current location in Yamazaki. At that time, {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡大神}} (Hondawake-no-Mikoto) was enshrined as a secondary deity. A stone shrine (okumiya) remains on the summit of Takahatayama, and an information board at the mountain trailhead near {{ill|Genda Onsen|ja|源田温泉}} recounts this history. According to shrine records, the shrine’s origins trace back to the 11th year of Emperor Kinmei ({{ill|550|ja|550年}}?). During that time, Seoritsuhime was believed to have manifested on Takahatayama's summit. Seoritsuhime, identified as a deity born from the purification of {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊耶那岐命}} at Awagihara, was venerated for her ability to cleanse impurities and pacify disturbances. === Historical Overview === As recorded in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}, the shrine was granted the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 14th year of {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} ({{ill|847|ja|847年}}). According to the {{ill|Ruijū Kokushi|ja|類聚国史}}, the shrine's rank was elevated to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 11th year of {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} ({{ill|869|ja|869年}}). In {{ill|927|ja|927年}}, the shrine was listed as a {{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} and became the main shrine of the three {{ill|Shikinai shrines|ja|式内社}} in the Asaka District, receiving deep veneration from both rulers and local residents. It was also designated the total shrine (sōsha) for the {{ill|33 communities of Asaka|ja|安積三十三郷}}. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, {{ill|Kudō Suketsune|ja|工藤祐経}}, appointed as local governor, introduced deities from the {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋大社}} and other shrines in Izu Province as subordinate shrines. The shrine was further restored by local rulers such as {{ill|Ashina clan|ja|蘆名氏}} and {{ill|Gamo Ujisato|ja|蒲生氏郷}}, and it received land grants and other support. === typeings === * {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} 14 ({{ill|847|ja|847年}}): Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}) * {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} 11 ({{ill|869|ja|869年}}): Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}) == Shrine Grounds == === Main Shrine === The shrine comprises a haiden, heiden, and a covered three-bay honden in {{ill|Miya-zukuri|ja|流造}} style. The honden features three doors, symbolizing the deities enshrined. Presently, the shrine honors two deities, with one seat left vacant. File:Honden of Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Honden (Three-bay miya-zukuri style) File:Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Haiden === Torii and Approach === A stream flows beneath the torii. The approach features memorial stones, subsidiary shrines, and a shrine office. File:Suitengu shrine of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Water deity shrine File:Main approach to Unakorowake-jinja 2.JPG|Main approach File:Torii gate of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Torii === Subsidiary Shrines === The shrine precinct includes various stone shrines dedicated to deities such as {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋神社}}, {{ill|Izu-san Shrine|ja|伊豆山神社}}, {{ill|Hakone Shrine|ja|箱根神社}}, and others. == Festivals == The Spring Festival is held annually from {{ill|April 2|ja|4月2日}}, and the Autumn Festival occurs from {{ill|September 18|ja|9月18日}}. Historical records indicate that events such as horseback archery were once part of the celebrations. == Access == '''Address''' * {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}, {{ill|Kōriyama|ja|郡山市}}, Mihota-machi Hachiman, Kamino-dai 76 === Public Transportation === * From {{ill|Koriyama Station|ja|郡山駅}}, take the No. 2 bus bound for Nagahama (approx. 35 minutes). Alight at Mihota Community Center and walk immediately. === By Car === * About 10 minutes from {{ill|Koriyama-Minami IC|ja|郡山南インターチェンジ}}. == References == * ''Asaka no Jinjashi'' (Fukushima Prefecture Shrine Bureau, Kōriyama Branch, 2001), pp. 181–183. * ''Zenkoku Jinja Meikan, Vol. 1'' (National Shrine Directory, 1977). == External Links == * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/271001.html Haiden (Worship Hall) | location = {{ill|Kōriyama, Fukushima|ja|郡山市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|37|21|35.36|N|140|17|18.46|E|type:landmark_region:JP-07|display=inline,title|name=Unakorowake Shrine}} | deity = {{ill|Seoritsuhime|ja|瀬織津姫|1=Seoritsu-Hime}} | type = {{ill|Shikinai shrine|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}})
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} | founded = {{ill|550|ja|550年}} (11th year of Emperor Kinmei?)
{{ill|782|ja|782年}} (Enryaku 1, as per records) | architecture = {{ill|Miya-zukuri|ja|流造}} (three-bay style) | other_names = Aiden Hachiman Shrine (相殿八幡神社) | festivals = {{ill|April 2|ja|4月2日}} (Spring Festival)
{{ill|September 18|ja|9月18日}} (Autumn Festival) }} '''Unakorowake Shrine''' (宇奈己呂和気神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Kōriyama|ja|郡山市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai shrine|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}}), and its former shrine ranking under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. [[Unakoro Waki Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''{{ill|Seoritsuhime|ja|瀬織津比売命}}''' - One of the {{ill|Haraedo-no-Ōkami|ja|祓戸大神}} '''Secondary deity''' * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡神}}: Hondawake-no-Mikoto ({{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇}}) == History == === Founding === According to ancient records, during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Kōnin|ja|光仁天皇}}, disturbances caused by the {{ill|Emishi|ja|蝦夷}} were widespread in the Mutsu Province. In the first year of {{ill|Ten'ō|ja|天応}} ({{ill|781|ja|781年}}), the court dispatched {{ill|Fujiwara no Oguro|ja|藤原小黒麿}} as inspector of Mutsu and Dewa, but he failed to suppress the unrest. The following year, in the first year of {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦}} ({{ill|782|ja|782年}}), the newly enthroned {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇}} sent {{ill|Ōtomo no Yakamochi|ja|大伴家持}} to the region as an inspector and commander. After seeking divine guidance on {{ill|Takahatayama|ja|高旗山}}, Yakamochi established a shrine to enshrine Seoritsuhime, whose divine power reportedly aided in subduing the unrest. Later, in the 3rd year of Enryaku ({{ill|784|ja|784年}}), the shrine was moved from Takahatayama to its current location in Yamazaki. At that time, {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡大神}} (Hondawake-no-Mikoto) was enshrined as a secondary deity. A stone shrine (okumiya) remains on the summit of Takahatayama, and an information board at the mountain trailhead near {{ill|Genda Onsen|ja|源田温泉}} recounts this history. According to shrine records, the shrine’s origins trace back to the 11th year of Emperor Kinmei ({{ill|550|ja|550年}}?). During that time, Seoritsuhime was believed to have manifested on Takahatayama's summit. Seoritsuhime, identified as a deity born from the purification of {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊耶那岐命}} at Awagihara, was venerated for her ability to cleanse impurities and pacify disturbances. === Historical Overview === As recorded in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}, the shrine was granted the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 14th year of {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} ({{ill|847|ja|847年}}). According to the {{ill|Ruijū Kokushi|ja|類聚国史}}, the shrine's rank was elevated to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 11th year of {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} ({{ill|869|ja|869年}}). In {{ill|927|ja|927年}}, the shrine was listed as a {{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} and became the main shrine of the three {{ill|Shikinai shrines|ja|式内社}} in the Asaka District, receiving deep veneration from both rulers and local residents. It was also designated the total shrine (sōsha) for the {{ill|33 communities of Asaka|ja|安積三十三郷}}. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, {{ill|Kudō Suketsune|ja|工藤祐経}}, appointed as local governor, introduced deities from the {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋大社}} and other shrines in Izu Province as subordinate shrines. The shrine was further restored by local rulers such as {{ill|Ashina clan|ja|蘆名氏}} and {{ill|Gamo Ujisato|ja|蒲生氏郷}}, and it received land grants and other support. === typeings === * {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} 14 ({{ill|847|ja|847年}}): Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}) * {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} 11 ({{ill|869|ja|869年}}): Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}) == Shrine Grounds == === Main Shrine === The shrine comprises a haiden, heiden, and a covered three-bay honden in {{ill|Miya-zukuri|ja|流造}} style. The honden features three doors, symbolizing the deities enshrined. Presently, the shrine honors two deities, with one seat left vacant. File:Honden of Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Honden (Three-bay miya-zukuri style) File:Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Haiden === Torii and Approach === A stream flows beneath the torii. The approach features memorial stones, subsidiary shrines, and a shrine office. File:Suitengu shrine of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Water deity shrine File:Main approach to Unakorowake-jinja 2.JPG|Main approach File:Torii gate of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Torii === Subsidiary Shrines === The shrine precinct includes various stone shrines dedicated to deities such as {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋神社}}, {{ill|Izu-san Shrine|ja|伊豆山神社}}, {{ill|Hakone Shrine|ja|箱根神社}}, and others. == Festivals == The Spring Festival is held annually from {{ill|April 2|ja|4月2日}}, and the Autumn Festival occurs from {{ill|September 18|ja|9月18日}}. Historical records indicate that events such as horseback archery were once part of the celebrations. == Access == '''Address''' * {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}, {{ill|Kōriyama|ja|郡山市}}, Mihota-machi Hachiman, Kamino-dai 76 === Public Transportation === * From {{ill|Koriyama Station|ja|郡山駅}}, take the No. 2 bus bound for Nagahama (approx. 35 minutes). Alight at Mihota Community Center and walk immediately. === By Car === * About 10 minutes from {{ill|Koriyama-Minami IC|ja|郡山南インターチェンジ}}. == References == * ''Asaka no Jinjashi'' (Fukushima Prefecture Shrine Bureau, Kōriyama Branch, 2001), pp. 181–183. * ''Zenkoku Jinja Meikan, Vol. 1'' (National Shrine Directory, 1977). == External Links == * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/271001.html Unakorowake Shrine] (Kokugakuin University, 21st Century COE Program) [[Category:Shrines in Kōriyama]] [[Category:Sōsha]] [[Category:Myōjin taisha]] [[Category:Shikinai shrines of Mutsu Province]] [[Category:Former gōsha shrines of Fukushima Prefecture]] [[ja:宇奈己呂和気神社]] Here is a list of provincial soja including this one * {{ill|Akasaka Uenoyama Shrine|ja|赤坂上之山神社}} * {{ill|Unakoro Waki Shrine|ja|宇奈己呂和気神社}} * {{ill|Ono Shrine (Ritto City)|ja|大野神社 (栗東市)}} * {{ill|Ogami Shrine (Tonami City)|ja|雄神神社 (砺波市)}} * {{ill|Kainan Shrine|ja|海南神社}} * {{ill|Katsushika Shrine|ja|葛飾神社}} * {{ill|Katsube Shrine|ja|勝部神社}} * {{ill|Mukuhashi Shrine|ja|椋橋総社}} * {{ill|Kotai Jingu (Fujisawa City)|ja|皇大神宮 (藤沢市)}} * {{ill|Gosho Shrine (Sammu City)|ja|五所神社 (山武市)}} * {{ill|Sakata Shinmei Shrine|ja|坂田神明宮}} * {{ill|Shinkai Sansha Shrine|ja|新海三社神社}} * {{ill|Sazama Shrine (Daito City)|ja|坐摩神社 (大東市)}} * {{ill|Kenda Suga Shrine|ja|健田須賀神社}} * {{ill|Tachibana Shrine (Kawasaki City)|ja|橘樹神社 (川崎市)}} * {{ill|Torakashi Shrine|ja|虎柏神社}} * {{ill|Nagao Shrine|ja|長尾神社}} * {{ill|Nanba Shrine|ja|難波神社|de|Namba-Schrein|fr|Namba-jinja|simple}} (may have historically been a provincal one) * {{ill|Arayaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine|ja|新屋坐天照御魂神社}} * {{ill|Nogi Shrine (Tokyo)|lt=Nogi Shrine|ja|能義神社}} * {{ill|Hotaka Shrine|ja|穂高神社|simple}} * {{ill|Washinomiya Shrine|ja|鷲宮神社}} ==References== {{ill|September 18|ja|9月18日}} (Autumn Festival) }} '''Unakorowake Shrine''' (宇奈己呂和気神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Kōriyama|ja|郡山市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai shrine|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}}), and its former shrine ranking under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. [[Unakoro Waki Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''{{ill|Seoritsuhime|ja|瀬織津比売命}}''' - One of the {{ill|Haraedo-no-Ōkami|ja|祓戸大神}} '''Secondary deity''' * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡神}}: Hondawake-no-Mikoto ({{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇}}) == History == === Founding === According to ancient records, during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Kōnin|ja|光仁天皇}}, disturbances caused by the {{ill|Emishi|ja|蝦夷}} were widespread in the Mutsu Province. In the first year of {{ill|Ten'ō|ja|天応}} ({{ill|781|ja|781年}}), the court dispatched {{ill|Fujiwara no Oguro|ja|藤原小黒麿}} as inspector of Mutsu and Dewa, but he failed to suppress the unrest. The following year, in the first year of {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦}} ({{ill|782|ja|782年}}), the newly enthroned {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇}} sent {{ill|Ōtomo no Yakamochi|ja|大伴家持}} to the region as an inspector and commander. After seeking divine guidance on {{ill|Takahatayama|ja|高旗山}}, Yakamochi established a shrine to enshrine Seoritsuhime, whose divine power reportedly aided in subduing the unrest. Later, in the 3rd year of Enryaku ({{ill|784|ja|784年}}), the shrine was moved from Takahatayama to its current location in Yamazaki. At that time, {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡大神}} (Hondawake-no-Mikoto) was enshrined as a secondary deity. A stone shrine (okumiya) remains on the summit of Takahatayama, and an information board at the mountain trailhead near {{ill|Genda Onsen|ja|源田温泉}} recounts this history. According to shrine records, the shrine’s origins trace back to the 11th year of Emperor Kinmei ({{ill|550|ja|550年}}?). During that time, Seoritsuhime was believed to have manifested on Takahatayama's summit. Seoritsuhime, identified as a deity born from the purification of {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊耶那岐命}} at Awagihara, was venerated for her ability to cleanse impurities and pacify disturbances. === Historical Overview === As recorded in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}, the shrine was granted the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 14th year of {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} ({{ill|847|ja|847年}}). According to the {{ill|Ruijū Kokushi|ja|類聚国史}}, the shrine's rank was elevated to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 11th year of {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} ({{ill|869|ja|869年}}). In {{ill|927|ja|927年}}, the shrine was listed as a {{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} and became the main shrine of the three {{ill|Shikinai shrines|ja|式内社}} in the Asaka District, receiving deep veneration from both rulers and local residents. It was also designated the total shrine (sōsha) for the {{ill|33 communities of Asaka|ja|安積三十三郷}}. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, {{ill|Kudō Suketsune|ja|工藤祐経}}, appointed as local governor, introduced deities from the {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋大社}} and other shrines in Izu Province as subordinate shrines. The shrine was further restored by local rulers such as {{ill|Ashina clan|ja|蘆名氏}} and {{ill|Gamo Ujisato|ja|蒲生氏郷}}, and it received land grants and other support. === typeings === * {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} 14 ({{ill|847|ja|847年}}): Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}) * {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} 11 ({{ill|869|ja|869年}}): Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}) == Shrine Grounds == === Main Shrine === The shrine comprises a haiden, heiden, and a covered three-bay honden in {{ill|Miya-zukuri|ja|流造}} style. The honden features three doors, symbolizing the deities enshrined. Presently, the shrine honors two deities, with one seat left vacant. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''{{ill|Seoritsuhime|ja|瀬織津比売命}}''' - One of the {{ill|Haraedo-no-Ōkami|ja|祓戸大神}} '''Secondary deity''' * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡神}}: Hondawake-no-Mikoto ({{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇}}) == History == === Founding === According to ancient records, during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Kōnin|ja|光仁天皇}}, disturbances caused by the {{ill|Emishi|ja|蝦夷}} were widespread in the Mutsu Province. In the first year of {{ill|Ten'ō|ja|天応}} ({{ill|781|ja|781年}}), the court dispatched {{ill|Fujiwara no Oguro|ja|藤原小黒麿}} as inspector of Mutsu and Dewa, but he failed to suppress the unrest. The following year, in the first year of {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦}} ({{ill|782|ja|782年}}), the newly enthroned {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇}} sent {{ill|Ōtomo no Yakamochi|ja|大伴家持}} to the region as an inspector and commander. After seeking divine guidance on {{ill|Takahatayama|ja|高旗山}}, Yakamochi established a shrine to enshrine Seoritsuhime, whose divine power reportedly aided in subduing the unrest. Later, in the 3rd year of Enryaku ({{ill|784|ja|784年}}), the shrine was moved from Takahatayama to its current location in Yamazaki. At that time, {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡大神}} (Hondawake-no-Mikoto) was enshrined as a secondary deity. A stone shrine (okumiya) remains on the summit of Takahatayama, and an information board at the mountain trailhead near {{ill|Genda Onsen|ja|源田温泉}} recounts this history. According to shrine records, the shrine’s origins trace back to the 11th year of Emperor Kinmei ({{ill|550|ja|550年}}?). During that time, Seoritsuhime was believed to have manifested on Takahatayama's summit. Seoritsuhime, identified as a deity born from the purification of {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊耶那岐命}} at Awagihara, was venerated for her ability to cleanse impurities and pacify disturbances. === Historical Overview === As recorded in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}, the shrine was granted the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 14th year of {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} ({{ill|847|ja|847年}}). According to the {{ill|Ruijū Kokushi|ja|類聚国史}}, the shrine's rank was elevated to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 11th year of {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} ({{ill|869|ja|869年}}). In {{ill|927|ja|927年}}, the shrine was listed as a {{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} and became the main shrine of the three {{ill|Shikinai shrines|ja|式内社}} in the Asaka District, receiving deep veneration from both rulers and local residents. It was also designated the total shrine (sōsha) for the {{ill|33 communities of Asaka|ja|安積三十三郷}}. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, {{ill|Kudō Suketsune|ja|工藤祐経}}, appointed as local governor, introduced deities from the {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋大社}} and other shrines in Izu Province as subordinate shrines. The shrine was further restored by local rulers such as {{ill|Ashina clan|ja|蘆名氏}} and {{ill|Gamo Ujisato|ja|蒲生氏郷}}, and it received land grants and other support. === typeings === * {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} 14 ({{ill|847|ja|847年}}): Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}) * {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} 11 ({{ill|869|ja|869年}}): Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}) == Shrine Grounds == === Main Shrine === The shrine comprises a haiden, heiden, and a covered three-bay honden in {{ill|Miya-zukuri|ja|流造}} style. The honden features three doors, symbolizing the deities enshrined. Presently, the shrine honors two deities, with one seat left vacant. File:Honden of Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Honden (Three-bay miya-zukuri style) File:Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Haiden === Torii and Approach === A stream flows beneath the torii. The approach features memorial stones, subsidiary shrines, and a shrine office. File:Suitengu shrine of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Water deity shrine File:Main approach to Unakorowake-jinja 2.JPG|Main approach File:Torii gate of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Torii === Subsidiary Shrines === The shrine precinct includes various stone shrines dedicated to deities such as {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋神社}}, {{ill|Izu-san Shrine|ja|伊豆山神社}}, {{ill|Hakone Shrine|ja|箱根神社}}, and others. == Festivals == The Spring Festival is held annually from {{ill|April 2|ja|4月2日}}, and the Autumn Festival occurs from {{ill|September 18|ja|9月18日}}. Historical records indicate that events such as horseback archery were once part of the celebrations. == Access == '''Address''' * {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}, {{ill|Kōriyama|ja|郡山市}}, Mihota-machi Hachiman, Kamino-dai 76 === Public Transportation === * From {{ill|Koriyama Station|ja|郡山駅}}, take the No. 2 bus bound for Nagahama (approx. 35 minutes). {{ill|September 18|ja|9月18日}} (Autumn Festival) }} '''Unakorowake Shrine''' (宇奈己呂和気神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Kōriyama|ja|郡山市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai shrine|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}}), and its former shrine ranking under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. [[Unakoro Waki Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''{{ill|Seoritsuhime|ja|瀬織津比売命}}''' - One of the {{ill|Haraedo-no-Ōkami|ja|祓戸大神}} '''Secondary deity''' * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡神}}: Hondawake-no-Mikoto ({{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇}}) == History == === Founding === According to ancient records, during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Kōnin|ja|光仁天皇}}, disturbances caused by the {{ill|Emishi|ja|蝦夷}} were widespread in the Mutsu Province. In the first year of {{ill|Ten'ō|ja|天応}} ({{ill|781|ja|781st year }}), the court dispatched {{ill|Fujiwara no Oguro|ja|藤原小黒麿}} as inspector of Mutsu and Dewa, but he failed to suppress the unrest. The following year, in the first year of {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦}} ({{ill|782|ja|782年}}), the newly enthroned {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇}} sent {{ill|Ōtomo no Yakamochi|ja|大伴家持}} to the region as an inspector and commander. After seeking divine guidance on {{ill|Takahatayama|ja|高旗山}}, Yakamochi established a shrine to enshrine Seoritsuhime, whose divine power reportedly aided in subduing the unrest. Later, in the 3rd year of Enryaku ({{ill|784|ja|784年}}), the shrine was moved from Takahatayama to its current location in Yamazaki. At that time, {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡大神}} (Hondawake-no-Mikoto) was enshrined as a secondary deity. A stone shrine (okumiya) remains on the summit of Takahatayama, and an information board at the mountain trailhead near {{ill|Genda Onsen|ja|源田温泉}} recounts this history. According to shrine records, the shrine’s origins trace back to the 11th year of Emperor Kinmei ({{ill|550|ja|550年}}?). During that time, Seoritsuhime was believed to have manifested on Takahatayama's summit. Seoritsuhime, identified as a deity born from the purification of {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊耶那岐命}} at Awagihara, was venerated for her ability to cleanse impurities and pacify disturbances. === Historical Overview === As recorded in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}, the shrine was granted the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 14th year of {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} ({{ill|847|ja|847年}}). According to the {{ill|Ruijū Kokushi|ja|類聚国史}}, the shrine's rank was elevated to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 11th year of {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} ({{ill|869|ja|869年}}). In {{ill|927|ja|927年}}, the shrine was listed as a {{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} and became the main shrine of the three {{ill|Shikinai shrines|ja|式内社}} in the Asaka District, receiving deep veneration from both rulers and local residents. It was also designated the total shrine (sōsha) for the {{ill|33 communities of Asaka|ja|安積三十三郷}}. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, {{ill|Kudō Suketsune|ja|工藤祐経}}, appointed as local governor, introduced deities from the {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋大社}} and other shrines in Izu Province as subordinate shrines. The shrine was further restored by local rulers such as {{ill|Ashina clan|ja|蘆名氏}} and {{ill|Gamo Ujisato|ja|蒲生氏郷}}, and it received land grants and other support. === typeings === * {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} 14 ({{ill|847|ja|847年}}): Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}) * {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} 11 ({{ill|869|ja|869年}}): Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}) == Shrine Grounds == === Main Shrine === The shrine comprises a haiden, heiden, and a covered three-bay honden in {{ill|Miya-zukuri|ja|流造}} style. The honden features three doors, symbolizing the deities enshrined. Presently, the shrine honors two deities, with one seat left vacant. File:Honden of Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Honden (Three-bay miya-zukuri style) File:Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Haiden === Torii and Approach === A stream flows beneath the torii. The approach features memorial stones, subsidiary shrines, and a shrine office. File:Suitengu shrine of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Water deity shrine File:Main approach to Unakorowake-jinja 2.JPG|Main approach File:Torii gate of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Torii === Subsidiary Shrines === The shrine precinct includes various stone shrines dedicated to deities such as {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋神社}}, {{ill|Izu-san Shrine|ja|伊豆山神社}}, {{ill|Hakone Shrine|ja|箱根神社}}, and others. == Festivals == The Spring Festival is held annually from {{ill|April 2|ja|4月2日}}, and the Autumn Festival occurs from {{ill|September 18|ja|9月18日}}. Historical records indicate that events such as horseback archery were once part of the celebrations. == Access == '''Address''' * {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}, {{ill|Kōriyama|ja|郡山市}}, Mihota-machi Hachiman, Kamino-dai 76 === Public Transportation === * From {{ill|Koriyama Station|ja|郡山駅}}, take the No. 2 bus bound for Nagahama (approx. 35 minutes). Alight at Mihota Community Center and walk immediately. === By Car === * About 10 minutes from {{ill|Koriyama-Minami IC|ja|郡山南インターチェンジ}}. == References == * ''Asaka no Jinjashi'' (Fukushima Prefecture Shrine Bureau, Kōriyama Branch, 2001), pp. 181–183. * ''Zenkoku Jinja Meikan, Vol. 1'' (National Shrine Directory, 1977). == External Links == * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/271001.html Unakorowake Shrine] (Kokugakuin University, 21st Century COE Program) [[Category:Shrines in Kōriyama]] [[Category:Sōsha]] [[Category:Myōjin taisha]] [[Category:Shikinai shrines of Mutsu Province]] {{ill|September 18|ja|9月18日}} (Autumn Festival) }} '''Unakorowake Shrine''' (宇奈己呂和気神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Kōriyama|ja|郡山市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai shrine|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}}), and its former shrine ranking under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. [[Unakoro Waki Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''{{ill|Seoritsuhime|ja|瀬織津比売命}}''' - One of the {{ill|Haraedo-no-Ōkami|ja|祓戸大神}} '''Secondary deity''' * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡神}}: Hondawake-no-Mikoto ({{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇}}) == History == === Founding === According to ancient records, during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Kōnin|ja|光仁天皇}}, disturbances caused by the {{ill|Emishi|ja|蝦夷}} were widespread in the Mutsu Province. In the first year of {{ill|Ten'ō|ja|天応}} ({{ill|781|ja|781st year }}), the court dispatched {{ill|Fujiwara no Oguro|ja|藤原小黒麿}} as inspector of Mutsu and Dewa, but he failed to suppress the unrest. The following year, in the first year of {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦}} ({{ill|782|ja|782nd year }}), the newly enthroned {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇}} sent {{ill|Ōtomo no Yakamochi|ja|大伴家持}} to the region as an inspector and commander. After seeking divine guidance on {{ill|Takahatayama|ja|高旗山}}, Yakamochi established a shrine to enshrine Seoritsuhime, whose divine power reportedly aided in subduing the unrest. Later, in the 3rd year of Enryaku ({{ill|784|ja|784th year }}), the shrine was moved from Takahatayama to its current location in Yamazaki. At that time, {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡大神}} (Hondawake-no-Mikoto) was enshrined as a secondary deity. A stone shrine (okumiya) remains on the summit of Takahatayama, and an information board at the mountain trailhead near {{ill|Genda Onsen|ja|源田温泉}} recounts this history. According to shrine records, the shrine’s origins trace back to the 11th year of Emperor Kinmei ({{ill|550|ja|550年}}?). During that time, Seoritsuhime was believed to have manifested on Takahatayama's summit. Seoritsuhime, identified as a deity born from the purification of {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊耶那岐命}} at Awagihara, was venerated for her ability to cleanse impurities and pacify disturbances. === Historical Overview === As recorded in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}, the shrine was granted the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 14th year of {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} ({{ill|847|ja|847年}}). According to the {{ill|Ruijū Kokushi|ja|類聚国史}}, the shrine's rank was elevated to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 11th year of {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} ({{ill|869|ja|869年}}). In {{ill|927|ja|927年}}, the shrine was listed as a {{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} and became the main shrine of the three {{ill|Shikinai shrines|ja|式内社}} in the Asaka District, receiving deep veneration from both rulers and local residents. It was also designated the total shrine (sōsha) for the {{ill|33 communities of Asaka|ja|安積三十三郷}}. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, {{ill|Kudō Suketsune|ja|工藤祐経}}, appointed as local governor, introduced deities from the {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋大社}} and other shrines in Izu Province as subordinate shrines. The shrine was further restored by local rulers such as {{ill|Ashina clan|ja|蘆名氏}} and {{ill|Gamo Ujisato|ja|蒲生氏郷}}, and it received land grants and other support. === typeings === * {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} 14 ({{ill|847|ja|847年}}): Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}) * {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} 11 ({{ill|869|ja|869年}}): Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}) == Shrine Grounds == === Main Shrine === The shrine comprises a haiden, heiden, and a covered three-bay honden in {{ill|Miya-zukuri|ja|流造}} style. The honden features three doors, symbolizing the deities enshrined. Presently, the shrine honors two deities, with one seat left vacant. File:Honden of Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Honden (Three-bay miya-zukuri style) File:Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Haiden === Torii and Approach === A stream flows beneath the torii. The approach features memorial stones, subsidiary shrines, and a shrine office. It is a {{ill|Shikinai shrine|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}}), and its former shrine ranking under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. [[Unakoro Waki Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''{{ill|Seoritsuhime|ja|瀬織津比売命}}''' - One of the {{ill|Haraedo-no-Ōkami|ja|祓戸大神}} '''Secondary deity''' * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡神}}: Hondawake-no-Mikoto ({{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇}}) == History == === Founding === According to ancient records, during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Kōnin|ja|光仁天皇}}, disturbances caused by the {{ill|Emishi|ja|蝦夷}} were widespread in the Mutsu Province. In the first year of {{ill|Ten'ō|ja|天応}} ({{ill|781|ja|781st year }}), the court dispatched {{ill|Fujiwara no Oguro|ja|藤原小黒麿}} as inspector of Mutsu and Dewa, but he failed to suppress the unrest. The following year, in the first year of {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦}} ({{ill|782|ja|782nd year }}), the newly enthroned {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇}} sent {{ill|Ōtomo no Yakamochi|ja|大伴家持}} to the region as an inspector and commander. After seeking divine guidance on {{ill|Takahatayama|ja|高旗山}}, Yakamochi established a shrine to enshrine Seoritsuhime, whose divine power reportedly aided in subduing the unrest. Later, in the 3rd year of Enryaku ({{ill|784|ja|784th year }}), the shrine was moved from Takahatayama to its current location in Yamazaki. At that time, {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡大神}} (Hondawake-no-Mikoto) was enshrined as a secondary deity. A stone shrine (okumiya) remains on the summit of Takahatayama, and an information board at the mountain trailhead near {{ill|Genda Onsen|ja|源田温泉}} recounts this history. According to shrine records, the shrine’s origins trace back to the 11th year of Emperor Kinmei ({{ill|550|ja|550年}}?). During that time, Seoritsuhime was believed to have manifested on Takahatayama's summit. Seoritsuhime, identified as a deity born from the purification of {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊耶那岐命}} at Awagihara, was venerated for her ability to cleanse impurities and pacify disturbances. === Historical Overview === As recorded in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}, the shrine was granted the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 14th year of {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} ({{ill|847|ja|847th year }}). According to the {{ill|Ruijū Kokushi|ja|類聚国史}}, the shrine's rank was elevated to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 11th year of {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} ({{ill|869|ja|869年}}). In {{ill|927|ja|927th year }}, the shrine was listed as a {{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} and became the main shrine of the three {{ill|Shikinai shrines|ja|式内社}} in the Asaka District, receiving deep veneration from both rulers and local residents. It was also designated the total shrine (sōsha) for the {{ill|33 communities of Asaka|ja|安積三十三郷}}. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, {{ill|Kudō Suketsune|ja|工藤祐経}}, appointed as local governor, introduced deities from the {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋大社}} and other shrines in Izu Province as subordinate shrines. The shrine was further restored by local rulers such as {{ill|Ashina clan|ja|蘆名氏}} and {{ill|Gamo Ujisato|ja|蒲生氏郷}}, and it received land grants and other support. === typeings === * {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} 14 ({{ill|847|ja|847th year }}): Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}) * {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} 11 ({{ill|869|ja|869年}}): Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}) == Shrine Grounds == === Main Shrine === The shrine comprises a haiden, heiden, and a covered three-bay honden in {{ill|Miya-zukuri|ja|流造}} style. The honden features three doors, symbolizing the deities enshrined. Presently, the shrine honors two deities, with one seat left vacant. File:Honden of Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Honden (Three-bay miya-zukuri style) File:Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Haiden === Torii and Approach === A stream flows beneath the torii. The approach features memorial stones, subsidiary shrines, and a shrine office. File:Suitengu shrine of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Water deity shrine File:Main approach to Unakorowake-jinja 2.JPG|Main approach File:Torii gate of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Torii === Subsidiary Shrines === The shrine precinct includes various stone shrines dedicated to deities such as {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋神社}}, {{ill|Izu-san Shrine|ja|伊豆山神社}}, {{ill|Hakone Shrine|ja|箱根神社}}, and others. == Festivals == The Spring Festival is held annually from {{ill|April 2|ja|4月2日}}, and the Autumn Festival occurs from {{ill|September 18|ja|9月18日}}. Historical records indicate that events such as horseback archery were once part of the celebrations. == Access == '''Address''' * {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}, {{ill|Kōriyama|ja|郡山市}}, Mihota-machi Hachiman, Kamino-dai 76 === Public Transportation === * From {{ill|Koriyama Station|ja|郡山駅}}, take the No. 2 bus bound for Nagahama (approx. 35 minutes). Alight at Mihota Community Center and walk immediately. === By Car === * About 10 minutes from {{ill|Koriyama-Minami IC|ja|郡山南インターチェンジ}}. == References == * ''Asaka no Jinjashi'' (Fukushima Prefecture Shrine Bureau, Kōriyama Branch, 2001), pp. 181–183. * ''Zenkoku Jinja Meikan, Vol. 1'' (National Shrine Directory, 1977). == External Links == * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/271001.html {{ill|September 18|ja|9月18日}} (Autumn Festival) }} '''Unakorowake Shrine''' (宇奈己呂和気神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Kōriyama|ja|郡山市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai shrine|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}}), and its former shrine ranking under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. [[Unakoro Waki Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''{{ill|Seoritsuhime|ja|瀬織津比売命}}''' - One of the {{ill|Haraedo-no-Ōkami|ja|祓戸大神}} '''Secondary deity''' * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡神}}: Hondawake-no-Mikoto ({{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇}}) == History == === Founding === According to ancient records, during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Kōnin|ja|光仁天皇}}, disturbances caused by the {{ill|Emishi|ja|蝦夷}} were widespread in the Mutsu Province. In the first year of {{ill|Ten'ō|ja|天応}} ({{ill|781|ja|781st year }}), the court dispatched {{ill|Fujiwara no Oguro|ja|藤原小黒麿}} as inspector of Mutsu and Dewa, but he failed to suppress the unrest. The following year, in the first year of {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦}} ({{ill|782|ja|782nd year }}), the newly enthroned {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇}} sent {{ill|Ōtomo no Yakamochi|ja|大伴家持}} to the region as an inspector and commander. After seeking divine guidance on {{ill|Takahatayama|ja|高旗山}}, Yakamochi established a shrine to enshrine Seoritsuhime, whose divine power reportedly aided in subduing the unrest. Later, in the 3rd year of Enryaku ({{ill|784|ja|784th year }}), the shrine was moved from Takahatayama to its current location in Yamazaki. At that time, {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡大神}} (Hondawake-no-Mikoto) was enshrined as a secondary deity. A stone shrine (okumiya) remains on the summit of Takahatayama, and an information board at the mountain trailhead near {{ill|Genda Onsen|ja|源田温泉}} recounts this history. According to shrine records, the shrine’s origins trace back to the 11th year of Emperor Kinmei ({{ill|550|ja|550th year }}?). During that time, Seoritsuhime was believed to have manifested on Takahatayama's summit. Seoritsuhime, identified as a deity born from the purification of {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊耶那岐命}} at Awagihara, was venerated for her ability to cleanse impurities and pacify disturbances. === Historical Overview === As recorded in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}, the shrine was granted the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 14th year of {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} ({{ill|847|ja|847th year }}). According to the {{ill|Ruijū Kokushi|ja|類聚国史}}, the shrine's rank was elevated to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 11th year of {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} ({{ill|869|ja|869th year }}). In {{ill|927|ja|927th year }}, the shrine was listed as a {{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} and became the main shrine of the three {{ill|Shikinai shrines|ja|式内社}} in the Asaka District, receiving deep veneration from both rulers and local residents. It was also designated the total shrine (sōsha) for the {{ill|33 communities of Asaka|ja|安積三十三郷}}. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, {{ill|Kudō Suketsune|ja|工藤祐経}}, appointed as local governor, introduced deities from the {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋大社}} and other shrines in Izu Province as subordinate shrines. The shrine was further restored by local rulers such as {{ill|Ashina clan|ja|蘆名氏}} and {{ill|Gamo Ujisato|ja|蒲生氏郷}}, and it received land grants and other support. === typeings === * {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} 14 ({{ill|847|ja|847th year }}): Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}) * {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} 11 ({{ill|869|ja|869th year }}): Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}) == Shrine Grounds == === Main Shrine === The shrine comprises a haiden, heiden, and a covered three-bay honden in {{ill|Miya-zukuri|ja|流造}} style. The honden features three doors, symbolizing the deities enshrined. Presently, the shrine honors two deities, with one seat left vacant. File:Honden of Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Honden (Three-bay miya-zukuri style) File:Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Haiden === Torii and Approach === A stream flows beneath the torii. The approach features memorial stones, subsidiary shrines, and a shrine office. File:Suitengu shrine of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Water deity shrine File:Main approach to Unakorowake-jinja 2.JPG|Main approach File:Torii gate of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Torii === Subsidiary Shrines === The shrine precinct includes various stone shrines dedicated to deities such as {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋神社}}, {{ill|Izu-san Shrine|ja|伊豆山神社}}, {{ill|Hakone Shrine|ja|箱根神社}}, and others. == Festivals == The Spring Festival is held annually from {{ill|April 2|ja|4月2日}}, and the Autumn Festival occurs from {{ill|September 18|ja|9月18日}}. Historical records indicate that events such as horseback archery were once part of the celebrations. == Access == '''Address''' * {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}, {{ill|Kōriyama|ja|郡山市}}, Mihota-machi Hachiman, Kamino-dai 76 === Public Transportation === * From {{ill|Koriyama Station|ja|郡山駅}}, take the No. 2 bus bound for Nagahama (approx. 35 minutes). Alight at Mihota Community Center and walk immediately. === By Car === * About 10 minutes from {{ill|Koriyama-Minami IC|ja|郡山南インターチェンジ}}. == References == * ''Asaka no Jinjashi'' (Fukushima Prefecture Shrine Bureau, Kōriyama Branch, 2001), pp. 181–183. * ''Zenkoku Jinja Meikan, Vol. 1'' (National Shrine Directory, 1977). == External Links == * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/271001.html Unakorowake Shrine] (Kokugakuin University, 21st Century COE Program) [[Category:Shrines in Kōriyama]] [[Category:Sōsha]] [[Category:Myōjin taisha]] [[Category:Shikinai shrines of Mutsu Province]] {{ill|September 18|ja|9月18日}} (Autumn Festival) }} '''Unakorowake Shrine''' (宇奈己呂和気神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Kōriyama|ja|郡山市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai shrine|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}}), and its former shrine ranking under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. [[Unakoro Waki Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''{{ill|Seoritsuhime|ja|瀬織津比売命}}''' - One of the {{ill|Haraedo-no-Ōkami|ja|祓戸大神}} '''Secondary deity''' * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡神}}: Hondawake-no-Mikoto ({{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇}}) == History == === Founding === According to ancient records, during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Kōnin|ja|光仁天皇}}, disturbances caused by the {{ill|Emishi|ja|蝦夷}} were widespread in the Mutsu Province. In the first year of {{ill|Ten'ō|ja|天応}} ({{ill|781|ja|781st year }}), the court dispatched {{ill|Fujiwara no Oguro|ja|藤原小黒麿}} as inspector of Mutsu and Dewa, but he failed to suppress the unrest. The following year, in the first year of {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦}} ({{ill|782|ja|782nd year }}), the newly enthroned {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇}} sent {{ill|Ōtomo no Yakamochi|ja|大伴家持}} to the region as an inspector and commander. After seeking divine guidance on {{ill|Takahatayama|ja|高旗山}}, Yakamochi established a shrine to enshrine Seoritsuhime, whose divine power reportedly aided in subduing the unrest. Later, in the 3rd year of Enryaku ({{ill|784|ja|784th year }}), the shrine was moved from Takahatayama to its current location in Yamazaki. At that time, {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡大神}} (Hondawake-no-Mikoto) was enshrined as a secondary deity. A stone shrine (okumiya) remains on the summit of Takahatayama, and an information board at the mountain trailhead near {{ill|Genda Onsen|ja|源田温泉}} recounts this history. According to shrine records, the shrine’s origins trace back to the 11th year of Emperor Kinmei ({{ill|550|ja|550th year }}?). During that time, Seoritsuhime was believed to have manifested on Takahatayama's summit. Seoritsuhime, identified as a deity born from the purification of {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊耶那岐命}} at Awagihara, was venerated for her ability to cleanse impurities and pacify disturbances. === Historical Overview === As recorded in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}, the shrine was granted the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 14th year of {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} ({{ill|847|ja|847th year }}). According to the {{ill|Ruijū Kokushi|ja|類聚国史}}, the shrine's rank was elevated to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 11th year of {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} ({{ill|869|ja|869th year }}). In {{ill|927|ja|927th year }}, the shrine was listed as a {{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} and became the main shrine of the three {{ill|Shikinai shrines|ja|式内社}} in the Asaka District, receiving deep veneration from both rulers and local residents. It was also designated the total shrine (sōsha) for the {{ill|33 communities of Asaka|ja|安積三十三郷}}. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, {{ill|Kudō Suketsune|ja|工藤祐経}}, appointed as local governor, introduced deities from the {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋大社}} and other shrines in Izu Province as subordinate shrines. The shrine was further restored by local rulers such as {{ill|Ashina clan|ja|蘆名氏}} and {{ill|Gamo Ujisato|ja|蒲生氏郷}}, and it received land grants and other support. === typeings === * {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} 14 ({{ill|847|ja|847th year }}): Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}) * {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} 11 ({{ill|869|ja|869th year }}): Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}) == Shrine Grounds == === Main Shrine === The shrine comprises a haiden, heiden, and a covered three-bay honden in {{ill|Miya-zukuri|ja|流造}} style. The honden features three doors, symbolizing the deities enshrined. Presently, the shrine honors two deities, with one seat left vacant. It is a {{ill|Shikinai shrine|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}}), and its former shrine ranking under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. [[Unakoro Waki Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''{{ill|Seoritsuhime|ja|瀬織津比売命}}''' - One of the {{ill|Haraedo-no-Ōkami|ja|祓戸大神}} '''Secondary deity''' * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡神}}: Hondawake-no-Mikoto ({{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇}}) == History == === Founding === According to ancient records, during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Kōnin|ja|光仁天皇}}, disturbances caused by the {{ill|Emishi|ja|蝦夷}} were widespread in the Mutsu Province. In the first year of {{ill|Ten'ō|ja|天応}} ({{ill|781|ja|781st year }}), the court dispatched {{ill|Fujiwara no Oguro|ja|藤原小黒麿}} as inspector of Mutsu and Dewa, but he failed to suppress the unrest. The following year, in the first year of {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦}} ({{ill|782|ja|782nd year }}), the newly enthroned {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇}} sent {{ill|Ōtomo no Yakamochi|ja|大伴家持}} to the region as an inspector and commander. After seeking divine guidance on {{ill|Takahatayama|ja|高旗山}}, Yakamochi established a shrine to enshrine Seoritsuhime, whose divine power reportedly aided in subduing the unrest. Later, in the 3rd year of Enryaku ({{ill|784|ja|784th year }}), the shrine was moved from Takahatayama to its current location in Yamazaki. At that time, {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡大神}} (Hondawake-no-Mikoto) was enshrined as a secondary deity. A stone shrine (okumiya) remains on the summit of Takahatayama, and an information board at the mountain trailhead near {{ill|Genda Onsen|ja|源田温泉}} recounts this history. According to shrine records, the shrine’s origins trace back to the 11th year of Emperor Kinmei ({{ill|550|ja|550th year }}?). During that time, Seoritsuhime was believed to have manifested on Takahatayama's summit. Seoritsuhime, identified as a deity born from the purification of {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊耶那岐命}} at Awagihara, was venerated for her ability to cleanse impurities and pacify disturbances. === Historical Overview === As recorded in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}, the shrine was granted the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 14th year of {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} ({{ill|847|ja|847th year }}). According to the {{ill|Ruijū Kokushi|ja|類聚国史}}, the shrine's rank was elevated to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 11th year of {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} ({{ill|869|ja|869th year }}). In {{ill|927|ja|927th year }}, the shrine was listed as a {{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} and became the main shrine of the three {{ill|Shikinai shrines|ja|式内社}} in the Asaka District, receiving deep veneration from both rulers and local residents. It was also designated the total shrine (sōsha) for the {{ill|33 communities of Asaka|ja|安積三十三郷}}. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, {{ill|Kudō Suketsune|ja|工藤祐経}}, appointed as local governor, introduced deities from the {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋大社}} and other shrines in Izu Province as subordinate shrines. The shrine was further restored by local rulers such as {{ill|Ashina clan|ja|蘆名氏}} and {{ill|Gamo Ujisato|ja|蒲生氏郷}}, and it received land grants and other support. === typeings === * {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} 14 ({{ill|847|ja|847th year }}): Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}) * {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} 11 ({{ill|869|ja|869th year }}): Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}) == Shrine Grounds == === Main Shrine === The shrine comprises a haiden, heiden, and a covered three-bay honden in {{ill|Miya-zukuri|ja|流造}} style. The honden features three doors, symbolizing the deities enshrined. Presently, the shrine honors two deities, with one seat left vacant. File:Honden of Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Honden (Three-bay miya-zukuri style) File:Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Haiden === Torii and Approach === A stream flows beneath the torii. The approach features memorial stones, subsidiary shrines, and a shrine office. File:Suitengu shrine of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Water deity shrine File:Main approach to Unakorowake-jinja 2.JPG|Main approach File:Torii gate of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Torii === Subsidiary Shrines === The shrine precinct includes various stone shrines dedicated to deities such as {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋神社}}, {{ill|Izu-san Shrine|ja|伊豆山神社}}, {{ill|Hakone Shrine|ja|箱根神社}}, and others. == Festivals == The Spring Festival is held annually from {{ill|April 2|ja|4月2日}}, and the Autumn Festival occurs from {{ill|September 18|ja|9月18日}}. Historical records indicate that events such as horseback archery were once part of the celebrations. == Access == '''Address''' * {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}, {{ill|Kōriyama|ja|郡山市}}, Mihota-machi Hachiman, Kamino-dai 76 === Public Transportation === * From {{ill|Koriyama Station|ja|郡山駅}}, take the No. 2 bus bound for Nagahama (approx. 35 minutes). Alight at Mihota Community Center and walk immediately. === By Car === * About 10 minutes from {{ill|Koriyama-Minami IC|ja|郡山南インターチェンジ}}. == References == * ''Asaka no Jinjashi'' (Fukushima Prefecture Shrine Bureau, Kōriyama Branch, 2001), pp. 181–183. * ''Zenkoku Jinja Meikan, Vol. 1'' (National Shrine Directory, 1977). == External Links == * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/271001.html {{ill|September 18|ja|9月18日}} (Autumn Festival) }} '''Unakorowake Shrine''' (宇奈己呂和気神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Kōriyama|ja|郡山市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai shrine|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}}), and its former shrine ranking under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. [[Unakoro Waki Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''{{ill|Seoritsuhime|ja|瀬織津比売命}}''' - One of the {{ill|Haraedo-no-Ōkami|ja|祓戸大神}} '''Secondary deity''' * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡神}}: Hondawake-no-Mikoto ({{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇}}) == History == === Founding === According to ancient records, during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Kōnin|ja|光仁天皇}}, disturbances caused by the {{ill|Emishi|ja|蝦夷}} were widespread in the Mutsu Province. In the first year of {{ill|Ten'ō|ja|天応}} ({{ill|781|ja|781st year }}), the court dispatched {{ill|Fujiwara no Oguro|ja|藤原小黒麿}} as inspector of Mutsu and Dewa, but he failed to suppress the unrest. The following year, in the first year of {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦}} ({{ill|782|ja|782nd year }}), the newly enthroned {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇}} sent {{ill|Ōtomo no Yakamochi|ja|大伴家持}} to the region as an inspector and commander. After seeking divine guidance on {{ill|Takahatayama|ja|高旗山}}, Yakamochi established a shrine to enshrine Seoritsuhime, whose divine power reportedly aided in subduing the unrest. Later, in the 3rd year of Enryaku ({{ill|784|ja|784th year }}), the shrine was moved from Takahatayama to its current location in Yamazaki. At that time, {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡大神}} (Hondawake-no-Mikoto) was enshrined as a secondary deity. A stone shrine (okumiya) remains on the summit of Takahatayama, and an information board at the mountain trailhead near {{ill|Genda Onsen|ja|源田温泉}} recounts this history. According to shrine records, the shrine’s origins trace back to the 11th year of Emperor Kinmei ({{ill|550|ja|550th year }}?). During that time, Seoritsuhime was believed to have manifested on Takahatayama's summit. Seoritsuhime, identified as a deity born from the purification of {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊耶那岐命}} at Awagihara, was venerated for her ability to cleanse impurities and pacify disturbances. === Historical Overview === As recorded in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}, the shrine was granted the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 14th year of {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} ({{ill|847|ja|847th year }}). According to the {{ill|Ruijū Kokushi|ja|類聚国史}}, the shrine's rank was elevated to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 11th year of {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} ({{ill|869|ja|869th year }}). In {{ill|927|ja|927th year }}, the shrine was listed as a {{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} and became the main shrine of the three {{ill|Shikinai shrines|ja|式内社}} in the Asaka District, receiving deep veneration from both rulers and local residents. It was also designated the total shrine (sōsha) for the {{ill|33 communities of Asaka|ja|安積三十三郷}}. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, {{ill|Kudō Suketsune|ja|工藤祐経}}, appointed as local governor, introduced deities from the {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋大社}} and other shrines in Izu Province as subordinate shrines. The shrine was further restored by local rulers such as {{ill|Ashina clan|ja|蘆名氏}} and {{ill|Gamo Ujisato|ja|蒲生氏郷}}, and it received land grants and other support. === typeings === * {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} 14 ({{ill|847|ja|847th year }}): Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}) * {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} 11 ({{ill|869|ja|869th year }}): Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}) == Shrine Grounds == === Main Shrine === The shrine comprises a haiden, heiden, and a covered three-bay honden in {{ill|Miya-zukuri|ja|流造}} style. The honden features three doors, symbolizing the deities enshrined. Presently, the shrine honors two deities, with one seat left vacant. File:Honden of Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Honden (Three-bay miya-zukuri style) File:Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Haiden === Torii and Approach === A stream flows beneath the torii. The approach features memorial stones, subsidiary shrines, and a shrine office. File:Suitengu shrine of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Water deity shrine File:Main approach to Unakorowake-jinja 2.JPG|Main approach File:Torii gate of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Torii === Subsidiary Shrines === The shrine precinct includes various stone shrines dedicated to deities such as {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋神社}}, {{ill|Izu-san Shrine|ja|伊豆山神社}}, {{ill|Hakone Shrine|ja|箱根神社}}, and others. == Festivals == The Spring Festival is held annually from {{ill|April 2|ja|4月2日}}, and the Autumn Festival occurs from {{ill|September 18|ja|9月18日}}. Historical records indicate that events such as horseback archery were once part of the celebrations. == Access == '''Address''' * {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}, {{ill|Kōriyama|ja|郡山市}}, Mihota-machi Hachiman, Kamino-dai 76 === Public Transportation === * From {{ill|Koriyama Station|ja|郡山駅}}, take the No. 2 bus bound for Nagahama (approx. 35 minutes). Alight at Mihota Community Center and walk immediately. === By Car === * About 10 minutes from {{ill|Koriyama-Minami IC|ja|郡山南インターチェンジ}}. == References == * ''Asaka no Jinjashi'' (Fukushima Prefecture Shrine Bureau, Kōriyama Branch, 2001), pp. 181–183. * ''Zenkoku Jinja Meikan, Vol. 1'' (National Shrine Directory, 1977). == External Links == * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/271001.html Unakorowake Shrine] (Kokugakuin University, 21st Century COE Program) [[Category:Shrines in Kōriyama]] [[Category:Sōsha]] [[Category:Myōjin taisha]] [[Category:Shikinai shrines of Mutsu Province]] The shrine was further restored by local rulers such as {{ill|Ashina clan|ja|蘆名氏}} and {{ill|Gamo Ujisato|ja|蒲生氏郷}}, and it received land grants and other support. === typeings === * {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} 14 ({{ill|847|ja|847th year }}): Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}) * {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} 11 ({{ill|869|ja|869th year }}): Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}) == Shrine Grounds == === Main Shrine === The shrine comprises a haiden, heiden, and a covered three-bay honden in {{ill|Miya-zukuri|ja|流造}} style. The honden features three doors, symbolizing the deities enshrined. Presently, the shrine honors two deities, with one seat left vacant. File:Honden of Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Honden (Three-bay miya-zukuri style) File:Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Haiden === Torii and Approach === A stream flows beneath the torii. The approach features memorial stones, subsidiary shrines, and a shrine office. File:Suitengu shrine of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Water deity shrine File:Main approach to Unakorowake-jinja 2.JPG|Main approach File:Torii gate of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Torii === Subsidiary Shrines === The shrine precinct includes various stone shrines dedicated to deities such as {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋神社}}, {{ill|Izu-san Shrine|ja|伊豆山神社}}, {{ill|Hakone Shrine|ja|箱根神社}}, and others. == Festivals == The Spring Festival is held annually from {{ill|April 2|ja|4月2日}}, and the Autumn Festival occurs from {{ill|September 18|ja|9月18日}}. Historical records indicate that events such as horseback archery were once part of the celebrations. == Access == '''Address''' * {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}, {{ill|Kōriyama|ja|郡山市}}, Mihota-machi Hachiman, Kamino-dai 76 === Public Transportation === * From {{ill|Koriyama Station|ja|郡山駅}}, take the No. 2 bus bound for Nagahama (approx. 35 minutes). Haiden (Worship Hall) | location = {{ill|Kōriyama, Fukushima|ja|郡山市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}, Japan | coordinates = {{Coord|37|21|35.36|N|140|17|18.46|E|type:landmark_region:JP-07|display=inline,title|name=Unakorowake Shrine}} | deity = {{ill|Seoritsuhime|ja|瀬織津姫|1=Seoritsu-Hime}} | type = {{ill|Shikinai shrine|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}})
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} | founded = {{ill|550|ja|550th year }} (11th year of Emperor Kinmei?)
{{ill|782|ja|782nd year }} (Enryaku 1, as per records) | architecture = {{ill|Miya-zukuri|ja|流造}} (three-bay style) | other_names = Aiden Hachiman Shrine (相殿八幡神社) | festivals = {{ill|April 2|ja|4月2日}} (Spring Festival)
{{ill|September 18|ja|9月18日}} (Autumn Festival) }} '''Unakorowake Shrine''' (宇奈己呂和気神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Kōriyama|ja|郡山市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai shrine|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}}), and its former shrine ranking under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. [[Unakoro Waki Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''{{ill|Seoritsuhime|ja|瀬織津比売命}}''' - One of the {{ill|Haraedo-no-Ōkami|ja|祓戸大神}} '''Secondary deity''' * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡神}}: Hondawake-no-Mikoto ({{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇}}) == History == === Founding === According to ancient records, during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Kōnin|ja|光仁天皇}}, disturbances caused by the {{ill|Emishi|ja|蝦夷}} were widespread in the Mutsu Province. In the first year of {{ill|Ten'ō|ja|天応}} ({{ill|781|ja|781st year }}), the court dispatched {{ill|Fujiwara no Oguro|ja|藤原小黒麿}} as inspector of Mutsu and Dewa, but he failed to suppress the unrest. The following year, in the first year of {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦}} ({{ill|782|ja|782nd year }}), the newly enthroned {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇}} sent {{ill|Ōtomo no Yakamochi|ja|大伴家持}} to the region as an inspector and commander. After seeking divine guidance on {{ill|Takahatayama|ja|高旗山}}, Yakamochi established a shrine to enshrine Seoritsuhime, whose divine power reportedly aided in subduing the unrest. Later, in the 3rd year of Enryaku ({{ill|784|ja|784th year }}), the shrine was moved from Takahatayama to its current location in Yamazaki. At that time, {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡大神}} (Hondawake-no-Mikoto) was enshrined as a secondary deity. A stone shrine (okumiya) remains on the summit of Takahatayama, and an information board at the mountain trailhead near {{ill|Genda Onsen|ja|源田温泉}} recounts this history. According to shrine records, the shrine’s origins trace back to the 11th year of Emperor Kinmei ({{ill|550|ja|550th year }}?). During that time, Seoritsuhime was believed to have manifested on Takahatayama's summit. Seoritsuhime, identified as a deity born from the purification of {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊耶那岐命}} at Awagihara, was venerated for her ability to cleanse impurities and pacify disturbances. === Historical Overview === As recorded in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}, the shrine was granted the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 14th year of {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} ({{ill|847|ja|847th year }}). According to the {{ill|Ruijū Kokushi|ja|類聚国史}}, the shrine's rank was elevated to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 11th year of {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} ({{ill|869|ja|869th year }}). In {{ill|927|ja|927th year }}, the shrine was listed as a {{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} and became the main shrine of the three {{ill|Shikinai shrines|ja|式内社}} in the Asaka District, receiving deep veneration from both rulers and local residents. It was also designated the total shrine (sōsha) for the {{ill|33 communities of Asaka|ja|安積三十三郷}}. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, {{ill|Kudō Suketsune|ja|工藤祐経}}, appointed as local governor, introduced deities from the {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋大社}} and other shrines in Izu Province as subordinate shrines. The shrine was further restored by local rulers such as {{ill|Ashina clan|ja|蘆名氏}} and {{ill|Gamo Ujisato|ja|蒲生氏郷}}, and it received land grants and other support. === typeings === * {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} 14 ({{ill|847|ja|847th year }}): Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}) * {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} 11 ({{ill|869|ja|869th year }}): Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}) == Shrine Grounds == === Main Shrine === The shrine comprises a haiden, heiden, and a covered three-bay honden in {{ill|Miya-zukuri|ja|流造}} style. The honden features three doors, symbolizing the deities enshrined. Presently, the shrine honors two deities, with one seat left vacant. File:Honden of Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Honden (Three-bay miya-zukuri style) File:Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Haiden === Torii and Approach === A stream flows beneath the torii. The approach features memorial stones, subsidiary shrines, and a shrine office. File:Suitengu shrine of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Water deity shrine File:Main approach to Unakorowake-jinja 2.JPG|Main approach File:Torii gate of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Torii === Subsidiary Shrines === The shrine precinct includes various stone shrines dedicated to deities such as {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋神社}}, {{ill|Izu-san Shrine|ja|伊豆山神社}}, {{ill|Hakone Shrine|ja|箱根神社}}, and others. == Festivals == The Spring Festival is held annually from {{ill|April 2|ja|4月2日}}, and the Autumn Festival occurs from {{ill|September 18|ja|9月18日}}. Historical records indicate that events such as horseback archery were once part of the celebrations. == Access == '''Address''' * {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}, {{ill|Kōriyama|ja|郡山市}}, Mihota-machi Hachiman, Kamino-dai 76 === Public Transportation === * From {{ill|Koriyama Station|ja|郡山駅}}, take the No. 2 bus bound for Nagahama (approx. 35 minutes). Alight at Mihota Community Center and walk immediately. === By Car === * About 10 minutes from {{ill|Koriyama-Minami IC|ja|郡山南インターチェンジ}}. == References == * ''Asaka no Jinjashi'' (Fukushima Prefecture Shrine Bureau, Kōriyama Branch, 2001), pp. 181–183. * ''Zenkoku Jinja Meikan, Vol. 1'' (National Shrine Directory, 1977). == External Links == * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/271001.html {{ill|September 18|ja|9月18日}} (Autumn Festival) }} '''Unakorowake Shrine''' (宇奈己呂和気神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Kōriyama|ja|郡山市}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai shrine|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}}), and its former shrine ranking under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}. [[Unakoro Waki Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''{{ill|Seoritsuhime|ja|瀬織津比売命}}''' - One of the {{ill|Haraedo-no-Ōkami|ja|祓戸大神}} '''Secondary deity''' * {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡神}}: Hondawake-no-Mikoto ({{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇}}) == History == === Founding === According to ancient records, during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Kōnin|ja|光仁天皇}}, disturbances caused by the {{ill|Emishi|ja|蝦夷}} were widespread in the Mutsu Province. In the first year of {{ill|Ten'ō|ja|天応}} ({{ill|781|ja|781st year }}), the court dispatched {{ill|Fujiwara no Oguro|ja|藤原小黒麿}} as inspector of Mutsu and Dewa, but he failed to suppress the unrest. The following year, in the first year of {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦}} ({{ill|782|ja|782nd year }}), the newly enthroned {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|ja|桓武天皇}} sent {{ill|Ōtomo no Yakamochi|ja|大伴家持}} to the region as an inspector and commander. After seeking divine guidance on {{ill|Takahatayama|ja|高旗山}}, Yakamochi established a shrine to enshrine Seoritsuhime, whose divine power reportedly aided in subduing the unrest. Later, in the 3rd year of Enryaku ({{ill|784|ja|784th year }}), the shrine was moved from Takahatayama to its current location in Yamazaki. At that time, {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡大神}} (Hondawake-no-Mikoto) was enshrined as a secondary deity. A stone shrine (okumiya) remains on the summit of Takahatayama, and an information board at the mountain trailhead near {{ill|Genda Onsen|ja|源田温泉}} recounts this history. According to shrine records, the shrine’s origins trace back to the 11th year of Emperor Kinmei ({{ill|550|ja|550th year }}?). During that time, Seoritsuhime was believed to have manifested on Takahatayama's summit. Seoritsuhime, identified as a deity born from the purification of {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊耶那岐命}} at Awagihara, was venerated for her ability to cleanse impurities and pacify disturbances. === Historical Overview === As recorded in the {{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}, the shrine was granted the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 14th year of {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} ({{ill|847|ja|847th year }}). According to the {{ill|Ruijū Kokushi|ja|類聚国史}}, the shrine's rank was elevated to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 11th year of {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} ({{ill|869|ja|869th year }}). In {{ill|927|ja|927th year }}, the shrine was listed as a {{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社}} in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} and became the main shrine of the three {{ill|Shikinai shrines|ja|式内社}} in the Asaka District, receiving deep veneration from both rulers and local residents. It was also designated the total shrine (sōsha) for the {{ill|33 communities of Asaka|ja|安積三十三郷}}. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, {{ill|Kudō Suketsune|ja|工藤祐経}}, appointed as local governor, introduced deities from the {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋大社}} and other shrines in Izu Province as subordinate shrines. The shrine was further restored by local rulers such as {{ill|Ashina clan|ja|蘆名氏}} and {{ill|Gamo Ujisato|ja|蒲生氏郷}}, and it received land grants and other support. === typeings === * {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|ja|承和}} 14 ({{ill|847|ja|847th year }}): Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Shoku Nihongi|ja|続日本後紀}}) * {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観}} 11 ({{ill|869|ja|869th year }}): Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}) == Shrine Grounds == === Main Shrine === The shrine comprises a haiden, heiden, and a covered three-bay honden in {{ill|Miya-zukuri|ja|流造}} style. The honden features three doors, symbolizing the deities enshrined. Presently, the shrine honors two deities, with one seat left vacant. File:Honden of Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Honden (Three-bay miya-zukuri style) File:Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Haiden === Torii and Approach === A stream flows beneath the torii. The approach features memorial stones, subsidiary shrines, and a shrine office. File:Suitengu shrine of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Water deity shrine File:Main approach to Unakorowake-jinja 2.JPG|Main approach File:Torii gate of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Torii === Subsidiary Shrines === The shrine precinct includes various stone shrines dedicated to deities such as {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋神社}}, {{ill|Izu-san Shrine|ja|伊豆山神社}}, {{ill|Hakone Shrine|ja|箱根神社}}, and others. == Festivals == The Spring Festival is held annually from {{ill|April 2|ja|4月2日}}, and the Autumn Festival occurs from {{ill|September 18|ja|9月18日}}. Historical records indicate that events such as horseback archery were once part of the celebrations. == Access == '''Address''' * {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|ja|福島県}}, {{ill|Kōriyama|ja|郡山市}}, Mihota-machi Hachiman, Kamino-dai 76 === Public Transportation === * From {{ill|Koriyama Station|ja|郡山駅}}, take the No. 2 bus bound for Nagahama (approx. 35 minutes). Alight at Mihota Community Center and walk immediately. === By Car === * About 10 minutes from {{ill|Koriyama-Minami IC|ja|郡山南インターチェンジ}}. == References == * ''Asaka no Jinjashi'' (Fukushima Prefecture Shrine Bureau, Kōriyama Branch, 2001), pp. 181–183. * ''Zenkoku Jinja Meikan, Vol. 1'' (National Shrine Directory, 1977). == External Links == * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/271001.html
