[[:en:September 18|September 18]] (Autumn Festival) }} '''Unakorowake Shrine''' (宇奈己呂和気神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Kōriyama|Kōriyama]], [[:en:Fukushima Prefecture|Fukushima Prefecture]]. It is designated as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin Taisha|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}), with its former status being that of a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. == Enshrined Deities == '''Chief deity''' * '''{{ill|Seoritsu-Hime|lt=Seoritsu-Hime|lt=Seoritsu Hime|ja|瀬織津姫|1=Seoritsu-Hime|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seoritsu Hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Seoritsu-Hime|qq=}}''' – One of the {{ill|Haraedo no Kami|lt=Haraedo no Kami|lt=Haraedo no Ōkami|ja|祓戸大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haraedo no Ōkami|qq=}} deities '''Subsidiary Deities''' * Hachiman God: Homutawake-no-Mikoto ([[:en:Emperor Ōjin|Emperor Ōjin]]) == History == === Establishment === According to old records of the shrine, during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Kōnin|Emperor Kōnin]], the land of Mutsu Province was rife with disturbances caused by the Emishi. In the first year of Ten'ō (781), the imperial court dispatched {{ill|Fujiwara no Kuro Maro|ja|藤原小黒麻呂|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Kuro Maro|qq=|1=Fujiwara no Oguromaro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11623210}} as the Inspector of Mutsu and Dewa Provinces (陸奥出羽按察使), but this effort yielded no results. The following year, in June of the first year of Enryaku (782), the newly enthroned Emperor Kanmu appointed [[:en:Ōtomo no Yakamochi|Ōtomo no Yakamochi]] as Inspector of Mutsu and Dewa Provinces and Commander of the Defense Forces (鎮守府将軍) and sent him to the region. However, the Emishi's strength was formidable, and Yakamochi ascended {{ill|Takahatayama|ja|高旗山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takahatayama|qq=|1=Takahata Yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q31470237}} to perform purification rituals and offer prayers to the deities. In response, divine spirits manifested, and miraculous signs appeared on the mountains of Asaka and {{ill|Yatsuhatayama|ja|八ツ旗山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yatsuhatayama|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Emboldened by these divine signs, Yakamochi led a campaign to pacify the Emishi. Through his efforts, the rebellions in Mutsu and Dewa Provinces were subdued, and peace was restored to the land. In gratitude for the divine assistance, Yakamochi constructed a magnificent shrine on the summit of Takahatayama to enshrine the guardian deity. Over time, the shrine fell into disrepair, prompting its relocation to its current site in Yamazaki in the third year of Enryaku (784), where a new shrine building was constructed. The deity {{ill|Hachiman Ōkami|ja|八幡大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman Ōkami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八幡神|1=Hachiman|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q261637}} (Homuda Wake no Mikoto) was also enshrined as a secondary deity. At the entrance to the mountain trail (pilgrimage path) leading to Takahatayama, near {{ill|Genda Onsen|ja|郡山市内の温泉#源田温泉（forest バン源田）|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Genda Onsen|qq=|1=Genda Onsen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11643189}}, there is a signboard detailing this history, and the summit still houses a stone shrine (okumiya) dedicated to {{ill|Unakiorowake Shrine|ja|宇奈己呂和気神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Unakiorowake Shrine|qq=|1=Unakorowake Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17217367}}. According to the shrine’s traditions, it was established in the 11th year of Emperor Kinmei's reign (circa 550 CE) when the deity {{ill|Seoritsu-Hime|lt=Seoritsu-Hime|lt=Seoritsu Hime|ja|瀬織津比売|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seoritsu Hime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 瀬織津姫}} manifested on the summit of Takahatayama in Asaka District. In the shrine's records, Seoritsu Hime is identified as the same deity as {{ill|Yaso Magatsuhi no Mikoto|ja|八十禍津日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yaso Magatsuhi no Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, born from the impurities cleansed by [[:en:Izanagi|Izanagi]] during his purification ritual at {{ill|Awagihara|ja|阿波岐原|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Awagihara|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Furthermore, Seoritsu Hime is associated with the "Ara-mitama" of Amaterasu Ōmikami, worshipped at the {{ill|Aramatsuri-no-Miya|ja|荒祭宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aramatsuri Shrine|qq=}} of [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] and [[:en:Hirota Shrine|Hirota Shrine]]. She is revered as a deity who purifies sins, impurities, and calamities in the world. This tradition reflects the prayers offered to Seoritsu Hime for the successful pacification of the Mutsu region, which had a fluctuating relationship with the Yamato court. The shrine is said to have been relocated from Takahatayama to its current location in the third year of Enryaku (784). === Historical Overview === According to the [[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Shoku Nihon Kōki]], in the 14th year of Shōwa (847), the deity of Unakiorowake Shrine was granted the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The [[:en:Ruijū Kokushi|Ruijū Kokushi]] records that in the 11th year of Jōgan (869), this Rank was elevated to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. Compiled in the 5th year of Enchō (927), the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]] designated Unakiorowake Shrine as a {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin Taisha|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, one of the major shrines of Asaka District’s three enshrined shrines. As the General Shrine (Sōsha) of the 33 Asaka villages, it commanded enduring respect and devotion from local leaders and residents. During the Kamakura period, [[:en:Kudō Suketsune|Kudō Suketsune]] was assigned as the local governor of Asaka District. He dispatched his son, {{ill|Asaka Suketaka|ja|安積祐長|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asaka Suketaka|qq=|1=Asaka no Suketaka|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q48761369}}, to manage the region. Recognizing the importance of “guardian worship” to secure public allegiance, Kudō Suketsune introduced deities from [[:en:Mishima Taisha|Mishima Taisha]], [[:en:Izusan Shrine|Izusan Shrine]], and [[:en:Hakone Shrine|Hakone Shrine]] into Asaka. Initially, these deities were enshrined as subsidiary gods of Unakiorowake Shrine rather than as principal deities, aiming to stabilize the populace and establish faith. Similar policies were adopted in the 6th year of Ōei (1399) when [[:en:Ashikaga Mitsukane|Ashikaga Mitsukane]] sent {{ill|Ashikaga Mitsunao|ja|足利満直|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashikaga Mitsunao|qq=|1=Ashikaga Mitsunao|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11636791}} and {{ill|Ashikaga Mitsusada|ja|足利満貞|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashikaga Mitsusada|qq=|1=Ashikaga Mitsusada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11636794}} to Mutsu and Dewa to solidify control. Upon arriving in Asaka District, Mitsunao sought to restore Unakiorowake Shrine. In the 9th year of Ōei (1402), he renovated the shrine buildings and grounds and appointed his retainer, Ōhara Yasunobu, as the shrine priest. The Ōhara family continues to serve as shrine priests to this day. After its relocation from Takahatayama, Hachiman Ōkami was enshrined as a secondary deity, leading to the shrine being known as “Hachiman Shrine” and later, during the Edo period, as “Aidan Hachiman Shrine.” Worship of the martial deity Hachiman Ōkami drew the reverence of local samurai. Historical records, including land donation documents granting 200 koku of land from lords such as Itō Taka-yuki, {{ill|Ashina Moritaka|ja|蘆名盛高|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashina Moritaka|qq=|1=Ashina Moritaka|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11625151}}, [[:en:Ashina Moriuji|Ashina Moriuji]], and [[:en:Gamō Ujisato|Gamo Ujisato]], as well as prayers from [[:en:Uesugi Kagekatsu|Uesugi Kagekatsu]] before the Battle of Sekigahara in Keichō 5 (1600), and the “Aidan Hachiman Documents,” have been preserved. In the 15th year of Meiji (1882), Unakiorowake Shrine was designated a village shrine (Gōsha). === Ranks === * Shōwa 14 (847): Elevated from no Rank to Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ([[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Shoku Nihon Kōki]]) * Jōgan 11 (869): Elevated from Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade, to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ([[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]) == Grounds == === Shrine buildings === The shrine complex includes the '''haiden''' (worship hall), '''heiden''' (offering hall), and the '''honden''' (main hall), which is a three-bay nagare-zukuri style structure with an enclosing roof. The '''honden''' features three doors, and according to shrine tradition, in addition to Seoritsu-Hime and Hondawake-no-Mikoto, Kasuga Ōkami ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天児屋命}}) was once enshrined here. Currently, the shrine enshrines only Seoritsu-Hime and Hondawake-no-Mikoto, leaving one seat vacant. File:Honden of Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|'''Honden'''
Three-bay nagare-zukuri style. File:Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|'''Haiden''' '''Interior of the Haiden''' The haiden displays large ema boards, including "Susanoo slaying Yamata-no-Orochi" and "Kato Kiyomasa hunting a tiger." Additionally, a plaque commemorates when [[:en:Itō Hirobumi|Itō Hirobumi]] visited the shrine during the Asaka Canal Completion tier 5]][[Category: ceremony and offered a heihaku fee of three yen. Other plaques, such as "Hachiman Shrine" and "Asaka Sōsha," are also displayed. File:Inside of Haiden of Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Interior of the haiden
The shrine mirror reveals the three doors of the honden. File:Inside of Haiden of Unakorowake-jinja 2.JPG|Plaques reading "Asaka Sōsha, Unakorowake Shrine" and "Hachiman Shrine." File:Inside of Haiden of Unakorowake-jinja 4.JPG|Plaque commemorating Itō Hirobumi’s donation: "Heihaku Fee: Three Yen, Councillor Itō Hirobumi." File:Ema board of "The story of Kiyomasa Kato hunting a tiger".JPG|Large ema: "Kato Kiyomasa hunting a tiger." File:Ema board of "The story of Susanowo slaying Yamata-no-Orochi".JPG|Large ema: "Susanoo slaying Yamata-no-Orochi." '''Other structures''' File:Kaguraden of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|'''Kaguraden''' (sacred dance stage) === Torii and approach === Passing through the '''torii''', visitors cross a small stream. To the west of the approach are a memorial stone and the '''Suitengū''' (dedicated to [[:en:Ame-no-Minakanushi|Ame-no-Minakanushi]]), while the shrine office lies to the right. File:Suitengu shrine of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Suitengū shrine within the grounds. File:Memorial stone of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Memorial stone along the approach. File:Main approach to Unakorowake-jinja 2.JPG|The shrine approach. File:Main approach to Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|The stone bridge and approach. File:Torii gate of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|The torii gate. == Auxiliary and subordinate shrines == To the west of the main shrine building lies the '''Yōsan Shrine''' (dedicated to Uka-no-Mitama-no-Kami and Wakumusubi-no-Kami) and a memorial shrine for the war dead. Additional stone shrines enshrine deities such as Mishima Shrine, Izusan Shrine, Hakone Shrine (all brought by Kudō Suketsune), Aosa Shrine, Yama Shrine, Inari Shrine, Kasuga Shrine, Tenman-gū, Itsukushima Shrine, and others. == Festivals == The spring grand festival takes place from April 2 to April 4, and the autumn grand festival occurs from September 18 to September 20. In the past, events such as yabusame (horseback archery) and mikoshi processions were held but were discontinued following the {{ill|Kakitsu Rebellion|ja|嘉吉の乱|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kakitsu Rebellion|qq=|1=Kakitsu Incident|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q5365139}} in 1441 and the [[:en:Kanshō famine|Great Famine of Chōroku and Kanshō]] in 1459. While attempts were made to revive the mikoshi processions under the protection of the Tanba clan during the Edo period, these rituals are no longer performed. == Access == '''location''' * 76 Kamino-dai, Hachiman, Mihota-machi, Kōriyama City, Fukushima Prefecture, Japan. === By bus === * From [[:en:Kōriyama Station (Fukushima)|Koriyama Station (Fukushima)]] (JR East Tōhoku Shinkansen), take the No. 2 bus bound for Naganuma (approx. 35 minutes) and alight at "Mihota Public Hall." The shrine is a short walk away. Check timetables for details. === By car === * About 10 minutes from {{ill|Kōriyama Minami Interchange (Fukushima)|ja|郡山南インターチェンジ (福島県)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōriyama Minami Interchange (Fukushima)|qq=|1=Koriyama-minami interchange|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11643156}}. == References == * ''Asaka no Jinja-shi'' (Fukushima Prefecture Shrine Office, Koriyama Branch, 2001), pp. 181–183, Unakorowake Shrine entry. * ''Zenkoku Jinja Meikan Vol. 1'' (National Shrine Directory Publishing Center, July 1977). == External links == {{Commonscat|Unakorowake-jinja}} * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/271001.html Unakorowake Shrine] (Kokugakuin University, 21st Century COE Program "Shinto and Shrine Archive"). {{Shinto}} {{Munakata Faith}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|宇奈己呂和気神社|version=85680187|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Koriyama]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Mutsu Province]] [[Category:Former Gō-sha in Fukushima Prefecture]] }} [[sn:Unojiro Wake Shrine]] [[ja:宇奈己呂和気神社]] [[sn:nojiro Wake Shrine]] [[sn:Unakoro Waki Shrine]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Koriyama]] {{Commons category|Unakorowake-jinja}}

[[:en:September 18|September 18]] (Autumn Festival) | location = {{ill|Kōriyama|qid=Q264206}} }} '''Unakorowake Shrine''' (宇奈己呂和気神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Kōriyama|Kōriyama]], [[:en:Fukushima Prefecture|Fukushima Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinai shrine|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai shrine|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin taisha|qq=|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Myōjin Taisha|WD=Q9610964}}), and its former shrine Ranking under the [[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]] was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. [[Unakoro Waki Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''{{ill|Seoritsu-Hime|lt=Seoritsu-Hime|lt=Seoritsuhime|ja|瀬織津比売命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seoritsuhime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' - One of the {{ill|Haraedo no Kami|lt=Haraedo no Kami|lt=Haraedo-no-Ōkami|ja|祓戸大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haraedo-no-Ōkami|qq=}} '''Secondary deity''' * [[:en:Hachiman|Hachiman]]: Hondawake-no-Mikoto ([[:en:Emperor Ōjin|Emperor Ōjin]]) == History == === Founding === According to ancient records, during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Kōnin|Emperor Kōnin]], disturbances caused by the [[:en:Emishi|Emishi]] were widespread in the Mutsu Province. In the first year of {{ill|Ten'ō|ja|天応 (日本)|1=Ten'ō|2=ja|3=天応 (日本)|qq=|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1373125}}{{citation needed|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten'ō|qq=}} ([[:en:781|781]]), the court dispatched {{ill|Fujiwara no Oguro|ja|藤原小黒麿|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Oguro|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} as inspector of Mutsu and Dewa, but he failed to suppress the unrest. The following year, in the first year of [[:en:Enryaku|Enryaku]] ([[:en:782|782]]), the newly enthroned [[:en:Emperor Kanmu|Emperor Kanmu]] sent [[:en:Ōtomo no Yakamochi|Ōtomo no Yakamochi]] to the region as an inspector and commander. After seeking divine guidance on {{ill|Takahatayama|ja|高旗山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takahatayama|qq=|1=Takahata Yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q31470237}}, Yakamochi established a shrine to enshrine Seoritsuhime, whose divine power reportedly aided in subduing the unrest. Later, in the 3rd year of Enryaku ([[:en:784|784]]), the shrine was moved from Takahatayama to its current location in Yamazaki. At that time, {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八幡神}} (Hondawake-no-Mikoto) was enshrined as a secondary deity. A stone shrine (okumiya) remains on the summit of Takahatayama, and an information board at the mountain trailhead near {{ill|Genda Onsen|ja|源田温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Genda Onsen|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} recounts this history. According to shrine records, the shrine’s origins trace back to the 11th year of Emperor Kinmei ([[:en:550|550]]?). During that time, Seoritsuhime was believed to have manifested on Takahatayama's summit. Seoritsuhime, identified as a deity born from the purification of {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊耶那岐命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} at Awagihara, was venerated for her ability to cleanse impurities and pacify disturbances. === Historical Overview === As recorded in the [[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Shoku Nihongi]], the shrine was granted the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 14th year of [[:en:Jōwa|Jōwa (Heian period)]] ([[:en:847|847]]). According to the [[:en:Ruijū Kokushi|Ruijū Kokushi]], the shrine's Rank was elevated to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 11th year of [[:en:Zhenguan|Jōgan]] ([[:en:869|869]]). In [[:en:927|927]], the shrine was listed as a {{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin taisha|qq=|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Myōjin Taisha|WD=Q9610964}} in the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]] and became the main shrine of the three {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} in the Asaka District, receiving deep veneration from both rulers and local residents. It was also designated the total shrine (sōsha) for the {{ill|33 communities of Asaka|ja|安積三十三郷|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/33 communities of Asaka|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. During the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]], [[:en:Kudō Suketsune|Kudō Suketsune]], appointed as local governor, introduced deities from the [[:en:Mishima Taisha|Mishima Taisha]] and other shrines in Izu Province as subordinate shrines. The shrine was further restored by local rulers such as [[:en:Ashina clan (Japan)|Ashina clan]] and [[:en:Gamō Ujisato|Gamo Ujisato]], and it received land grants and other support. === typeings === * [[:en:Jōwa|Jōwa (Heian period)]] 14 ([[:en:847|847]]): Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ([[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Shoku Nihongi]]) * [[:en:Zhenguan|Jōgan]] 11 ([[:en:869|869]]): Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ([[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]) == Shrine Grounds == === Main Shrine === The shrine comprises a haiden, heiden, and a covered three-bay honden in [[:en:Nagare-zukuri|Miya-zukuri]] style. The honden features three doors, symbolizing the deities enshrined. Presently, the shrine honors two deities, with one seat left vacant. File:Honden of Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Honden (Three-bay miya-zukuri style) File:Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Haiden === Torii and Approach === A stream flows beneath the torii. The approach features memorial stones, subsidiary shrines, and a shrine office. File:Suitengu shrine of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Water deity shrine File:Main approach to Unakorowake-jinja 2.JPG|Main approach File:Torii gate of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Torii === Subsidiary Shrines === The shrine precinct includes various stone shrines dedicated to deities such as {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mishima Taisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 三島神社}}, [[:en:Izusan Shrine|Izu-san Shrine]], [[:en:Hakone Shrine|Hakone Shrine]], and others. == Festivals == The Spring Festival is held annually from [[:en:April 2|April 2]], and the Autumn Festival occurs from [[:en:September 18|September 18]]. Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} |established = [[:en:Emperor Kinmei|Emperor Kinmei]] 11th year (550?)
[[:en:Enryaku|Enryaku]] 1 (782) (according to old records) |main building = Three-bay [[:en:Nagare-zukuri|Nagare-zukuri]] |alias = Hachiman Shrine (Aiden Hachiman Shrine) |pilgrimage = Sōja of the Asaka 33 Villages |annual festivals = [[:en:April 2|April 2]] (Spring Festival)
[[:en:September 18|September 18]] (Autumn Festival) }} '''Unakorowake Shrine''' (宇奈己呂和気神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Kōriyama|Kōriyama]], [[:en:Fukushima Prefecture|Fukushima Prefecture]]. It is designated as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin Taisha|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}), with its former status being that of a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. == Enshrined Deities == '''Chief deity''' * '''{{ill|Seoritsu-Hime|lt=Seoritsu-Hime|lt=Seoritsu Hime|ja|瀬織津姫|1=Seoritsu-Hime|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seoritsu Hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Seoritsu-Hime|qq=}}''' – One of the {{ill|Haraedo no Kami|lt=Haraedo no Kami|lt=Haraedo no Ōkami|ja|祓戸大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haraedo no Ōkami|qq=}} deities '''Subsidiary Deities''' * Hachiman God: Homutawake-no-Mikoto ([[:en:Emperor Ōjin|Emperor Ōjin]]) == History == === Establishment === According to old records of the shrine, during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Kōnin|Emperor Kōnin]], the land of Mutsu Province was rife with disturbances caused by the Emishi. In the first year of Ten'ō (781), the imperial court dispatched {{ill|Fujiwara no Kuro Maro|ja|藤原小黒麻呂|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Kuro Maro|qq=|1=Fujiwara no Oguromaro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11623210}} as the Inspector of Mutsu and Dewa Provinces (陸奥出羽按察使), but this effort yielded no results. The following year, in June of the first year of Enryaku (782), the newly enthroned Emperor Kanmu appointed [[:en:Ōtomo no Yakamochi|Ōtomo no Yakamochi]] as Inspector of Mutsu and Dewa Provinces and Commander of the Defense Forces (鎮守府将軍) and sent him to the region. However, the Emishi's strength was formidable, and Yakamochi ascended {{ill|Takahatayama|ja|高旗山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takahatayama|qq=|1=Takahata Yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q31470237}} to perform purification rituals and offer prayers to the deities. In response, divine spirits manifested, and miraculous signs appeared on the mountains of Asaka and {{ill|Yatsuhatayama|ja|八ツ旗山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yatsuhatayama|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Emboldened by these divine signs, Yakamochi led a campaign to pacify the Emishi. Through his efforts, the rebellions in Mutsu and Dewa Provinces were subdued, and peace was restored to the land. In gratitude for the divine assistance, Yakamochi constructed a magnificent shrine on the summit of Takahatayama to enshrine the guardian deity. Over time, the shrine fell into disrepair, prompting its relocation to its current site in Yamazaki in the third year of Enryaku (784), where a new shrine building was constructed. The deity {{ill|Hachiman Ōkami|ja|八幡大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman Ōkami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八幡神|1=Hachiman|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q261637}} (Homuda Wake no Mikoto) was also enshrined as a secondary deity. At the entrance to the mountain trail (pilgrimage path) leading to Takahatayama, near {{ill|Genda Onsen|ja|郡山市内の温泉#源田温泉（forest バン源田）|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Genda Onsen|qq=|1=Genda Onsen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11643189}}, there is a signboard detailing this history, and the summit still houses a stone shrine (okumiya) dedicated to {{ill|Unakiorowake Shrine|ja|宇奈己呂和気神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Unakiorowake Shrine|qq=|1=Unakorowake Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17217367}}. According to the shrine’s traditions, it was established in the 11th year of Emperor Kinmei's reign (circa 550 CE) when the deity {{ill|Seoritsu-Hime|lt=Seoritsu-Hime|lt=Seoritsu Hime|ja|瀬織津比売|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seoritsu Hime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 瀬織津姫}} manifested on the summit of Takahatayama in Asaka District. In the shrine's records, Seoritsu Hime is identified as the same deity as {{ill|Yaso Magatsuhi no Mikoto|ja|八十禍津日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yaso Magatsuhi no Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, born from the impurities cleansed by [[:en:Izanagi|Izanagi]] during his purification ritual at {{ill|Awagihara|ja|阿波岐原|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Awagihara|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Furthermore, Seoritsu Hime is associated with the "Ara-mitama" of Amaterasu Ōmikami, worshipped at the {{ill|Aramatsuri-no-Miya|ja|荒祭宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aramatsuri Shrine|qq=}} of [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] and [[:en:Hirota Shrine|Hirota Shrine]]. She is revered as a deity who purifies sins, impurities, and calamities in the world. This tradition reflects the prayers offered to Seoritsu Hime for the successful pacification of the Mutsu region, which had a fluctuating relationship with the Yamato court. The shrine is said to have been relocated from Takahatayama to its current location in the third year of Enryaku (784). === Historical Overview === According to the [[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Shoku Nihon Kōki]], in the 14th year of Shōwa (847), the deity of Unakiorowake Shrine was granted the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The [[:en:Ruijū Kokushi|Ruijū Kokushi]] records that in the 11th year of Jōgan (869), this Rank was elevated to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. Compiled in the 5th year of Enchō (927), the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]] designated Unakiorowake Shrine as a {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin Taisha|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, one of the major shrines of Asaka District’s three enshrined shrines. As the General Shrine (Sōsha) of the 33 Asaka villages, it commanded enduring respect and devotion from local leaders and residents. During the Kamakura period, [[:en:Kudō Suketsune|Kudō Suketsune]] was assigned as the local governor of Asaka District. He dispatched his son, {{ill|Asaka Suketaka|ja|安積祐長|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asaka Suketaka|qq=|1=Asaka no Suketaka|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q48761369}}, to manage the region. Recognizing the importance of “guardian worship” to secure public allegiance, Kudō Suketsune introduced deities from [[:en:Mishima Taisha|Mishima Taisha]], [[:en:Izusan Shrine|Izusan Shrine]], and [[:en:Hakone Shrine|Hakone Shrine]] into Asaka. Initially, these deities were enshrined as subsidiary gods of Unakiorowake Shrine rather than as principal deities, aiming to stabilize the populace and establish faith. Similar policies were adopted in the 6th year of Ōei (1399) when [[:en:Ashikaga Mitsukane|Ashikaga Mitsukane]] sent {{ill|Ashikaga Mitsunao|ja|足利満直|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashikaga Mitsunao|qq=|1=Ashikaga Mitsunao|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11636791}} and {{ill|Ashikaga Mitsusada|ja|足利満貞|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashikaga Mitsusada|qq=|1=Ashikaga Mitsusada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11636794}} to Mutsu and Dewa to solidify control. Upon arriving in Asaka District, Mitsunao sought to restore Unakiorowake Shrine. In the 9th year of Ōei (1402), he renovated the shrine buildings and grounds and appointed his retainer, Ōhara Yasunobu, as the shrine priest. The Ōhara family continues to serve as shrine priests to this day. After its relocation from Takahatayama, Hachiman Ōkami was enshrined as a secondary deity, leading to the shrine being known as “Hachiman Shrine” and later, during the Edo period, as “Aidan Hachiman Shrine.” Worship of the martial deity Hachiman Ōkami drew the reverence of local samurai. Historical records, including land donation documents granting 200 koku of land from lords such as Itō Taka-yuki, {{ill|Ashina Moritaka|ja|蘆名盛高|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashina Moritaka|qq=|1=Ashina Moritaka|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11625151}}, [[:en:Ashina Moriuji|Ashina Moriuji]], and [[:en:Gamō Ujisato|Gamo Ujisato]], as well as prayers from [[:en:Uesugi Kagekatsu|Uesugi Kagekatsu]] before the Battle of Sekigahara in Keichō 5 (1600), and the “Aidan Hachiman Documents,” have been preserved. In the 15th year of Meiji (1882), Unakiorowake Shrine was designated a village shrine (Gōsha). === Ranks === * Shōwa 14 (847): Elevated from no Rank to Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ([[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Shoku Nihon Kōki]]) * Jōgan 11 (869): Elevated from Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade, to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ([[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]) == Grounds == === Shrine buildings === The shrine complex includes the '''haiden''' (worship hall), '''heiden''' (offering hall), and the '''honden''' (main hall), which is a three-bay nagare-zukuri style structure with an enclosing roof. The '''honden''' features three doors, and according to shrine tradition, in addition to Seoritsu-Hime and Hondawake-no-Mikoto, Kasuga Ōkami ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天児屋命}}) was once enshrined here. Currently, the shrine enshrines only Seoritsu-Hime and Hondawake-no-Mikoto, leaving one seat vacant. File:Honden of Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|'''Honden'''
Three-bay nagare-zukuri style. File:Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|'''Haiden''' '''Interior of the Haiden''' The haiden displays large ema boards, including "Susanoo slaying Yamata-no-Orochi" and "Kato Kiyomasa hunting a tiger." Additionally, a plaque commemorates when [[:en:Itō Hirobumi|Itō Hirobumi]] visited the shrine during the Asaka Canal Completion tier 5]][[Category: ceremony and offered a heihaku fee of three yen. Other plaques, such as "Hachiman Shrine" and "Asaka Sōsha," are also displayed. File:Inside of Haiden of Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Interior of the haiden
The shrine mirror reveals the three doors of the honden. File:Inside of Haiden of Unakorowake-jinja 2.JPG|Plaques reading "Asaka Sōsha, Unakorowake Shrine" and "Hachiman Shrine." File:Inside of Haiden of Unakorowake-jinja 4.JPG|Plaque commemorating Itō Hirobumi’s donation: "Heihaku Fee: Three Yen, Councillor Itō Hirobumi." File:Ema board of "The story of Kiyomasa Kato hunting a tiger".JPG|Large ema: "Kato Kiyomasa hunting a tiger." File:Ema board of "The story of Susanowo slaying Yamata-no-Orochi".JPG|Large ema: "Susanoo slaying Yamata-no-Orochi." '''Other structures''' File:Kaguraden of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|'''Kaguraden''' (sacred dance stage) === Torii and approach === Passing through the '''torii''', visitors cross a small stream. To the west of the approach are a memorial stone and the '''Suitengū''' (dedicated to [[:en:Ame-no-Minakanushi|Ame-no-Minakanushi]]), while the shrine office lies to the right. File:Suitengu shrine of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Suitengū shrine within the grounds. File:Memorial stone of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Memorial stone along the approach. File:Main approach to Unakorowake-jinja 2.JPG|The shrine approach. File:Main approach to Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|The stone bridge and approach. File:Torii gate of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|The torii gate. == Auxiliary and subordinate shrines == To the west of the main shrine building lies the '''Yōsan Shrine''' (dedicated to Uka-no-Mitama-no-Kami and Wakumusubi-no-Kami) and a memorial shrine for the war dead. Additional stone shrines enshrine deities such as Mishima Shrine, Izusan Shrine, Hakone Shrine (all brought by Kudō Suketsune), Aosa Shrine, Yama Shrine, Inari Shrine, Kasuga Shrine, Tenman-gū, Itsukushima Shrine, and others. == Festivals == The spring grand festival takes place from April 2 to April 4, and the autumn grand festival occurs from September 18 to September 20. In the past, events such as yabusame (horseback archery) and mikoshi processions were held but were discontinued following the {{ill|Kakitsu Rebellion|ja|嘉吉の乱|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kakitsu Rebellion|qq=|1=Kakitsu Incident|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q5365139}} in 1441 and the [[:en:Kanshō famine|Great Famine of Chōroku and Kanshō]] in 1459. While attempts were made to revive the mikoshi processions under the protection of the Tanba clan during the Edo period, these rituals are no longer performed. == Access == '''location''' * 76 Kamino-dai, Hachiman, Mihota-machi, Kōriyama City, Fukushima Prefecture, Japan. === By bus === * From [[:en:Kōriyama Station (Fukushima)|Koriyama Station (Fukushima)]] (JR East Tōhoku Shinkansen), take the No. 2 bus bound for Naganuma (approx. 35 minutes) and alight at "Mihota Public Hall." The shrine is a short walk away. Check timetables for details. === By car === * About 10 minutes from {{ill|Kōriyama Minami Interchange (Fukushima)|ja|郡山南インターチェンジ (福島県)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōriyama Minami Interchange (Fukushima)|qq=|1=Koriyama-minami interchange|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11643156}}. == References == * ''Asaka no Jinja-shi'' (Fukushima Prefecture Shrine Office, Koriyama Branch, 2001), pp. 181–183, Unakorowake Shrine entry. * ''Zenkoku Jinja Meikan Vol. 1'' (National Shrine Directory Publishing Center, July 1977). == External links == {{Commonscat|Unakorowake-jinja}} * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/271001.html Unakorowake Shrine] (Kokugakuin University, 21st Century COE Program "Shinto and Shrine Archive"). {{Shinto}} {{Munakata Faith}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|宇奈己呂和気神社|version=85680187|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Koriyama]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Mutsu Province]] [[Category:Former Gō-sha in Fukushima Prefecture]] }} [[sn:Unojiro Wake Shrine]] [[ja:宇奈己呂和気神社]] [[sn:nojiro Wake Shrine]] [[sn:Unakoro Waki Shrine]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Koriyama]] {{Commons category|Unakorowake-jinja}}

[[:en:September 18|September 18]] (Autumn Festival) | location = {{ill|Kōriyama|qid=Q264206}} }} '''Unakorowake Shrine''' (宇奈己呂和気神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Kōriyama|Kōriyama]], [[:en:Fukushima Prefecture|Fukushima Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinai shrine|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai shrine|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin taisha|qq=|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Myōjin Taisha|WD=Q9610964}}), and its former shrine Ranking under the [[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]] was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. [[Unakoro Waki Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''{{ill|Seoritsu-hime|lt=Seoritsu-hime|lt=Seoritsuhime|ja|瀬織津比売命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seoritsuhime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' - One of the {{ill|Haraedo no Kami|lt=Haraedo no Kami|lt=Haraedo-no-Ōkami|ja|祓戸大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haraedo-no-Ōkami|qq=}} '''Secondary deity''' * [[:en:Hachiman|Hachiman]]: Hondawake-no-Mikoto ([[:en:Emperor Ōjin|Emperor Ōjin]]) == History == === Founding === According to ancient records, during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Kōnin|Emperor Kōnin]], disturbances caused by the [[:en:Emishi|Emishi]] were widespread in the Mutsu Province. In the first year of {{ill|Ten'ō|ja|天応 (日本)|1=Ten'ō|2=ja|3=天応 (日本)|qq=|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1373125}}{{citation needed|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten'ō|qq=}} ([[:en:781|781]]), the court dispatched {{ill|Fujiwara no Oguro|ja|藤原小黒麿|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Oguro|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} as inspector of Mutsu and Dewa, but he failed to suppress the unrest. The following year, in the first year of [[:en:Enryaku|Enryaku]] ([[:en:782|782]]), the newly enthroned [[:en:Emperor Kanmu|Emperor Kanmu]] sent [[:en:Ōtomo no Yakamochi|Ōtomo no Yakamochi]] to the region as an inspector and commander. After seeking divine guidance on {{ill|Takahatayama|ja|高旗山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takahatayama|qq=|1=Takahata Yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q31470237}}, Yakamochi established a shrine to enshrine Seoritsuhime, whose divine power reportedly aided in subduing the unrest. Later, in the 3rd year of Enryaku ([[:en:784|784]]), the shrine was moved from Takahatayama to its current location in Yamazaki. At that time, {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八幡神}} (Hondawake-no-Mikoto) was enshrined as a secondary deity. A stone shrine (okumiya) remains on the summit of Takahatayama, and an information board at the mountain trailhead near {{ill|Genda Onsen|ja|源田温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Genda Onsen|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} recounts this history. According to shrine records, the shrine’s origins trace back to the 11th year of Emperor Kinmei ([[:en:550|550]]?). During that time, Seoritsuhime was believed to have manifested on Takahatayama's summit. Seoritsuhime, identified as a deity born from the purification of {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊耶那岐命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} at Awagihara, was venerated for her ability to cleanse impurities and pacify disturbances. === Historical Overview === As recorded in the [[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Shoku Nihongi]], the shrine was granted the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 14th year of [[:en:Jōwa|Jōwa (Heian period)]] ([[:en:847|847]]). According to the [[:en:Ruijū Kokushi|Ruijū Kokushi]], the shrine's Rank was elevated to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 11th year of [[:en:Zhenguan|Jōgan]] ([[:en:869|869]]). In [[:en:927|927]], the shrine was listed as a {{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin taisha|qq=|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Myōjin Taisha|WD=Q9610964}} in the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]] and became the main shrine of the three {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} in the Asaka District, receiving deep veneration from both rulers and local residents. It was also designated the total shrine (sōsha) for the {{ill|33 communities of Asaka|ja|安積三十三郷|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/33 communities of Asaka|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. During the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]], [[:en:Kudō Suketsune|Kudō Suketsune]], appointed as local governor, introduced deities from the [[:en:Mishima Taisha|Mishima Taisha]] and other shrines in Izu Province as subordinate shrines. The shrine was further restored by local rulers such as [[:en:Ashina clan (Japan)|Ashina clan]] and [[:en:Gamō Ujisato|Gamo Ujisato]], and it received land grants and other support. === typeings === * [[:en:Jōwa|Jōwa (Heian period)]] 14 ([[:en:847|847]]): Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ([[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Shoku Nihongi]]) * [[:en:Zhenguan|Jōgan]] 11 ([[:en:869|869]]): Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ([[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]) == Shrine Grounds == === Main Shrine === The shrine comprises a haiden, heiden, and a covered three-bay honden in [[:en:Nagare-zukuri|Miya-zukuri]] style. The honden features three doors, symbolizing the deities enshrined. Presently, the shrine honors two deities, with one seat left vacant. File:Honden of Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Honden (Three-bay miya-zukuri style) File:Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Haiden === Torii and Approach === A stream flows beneath the torii. The approach features memorial stones, subsidiary shrines, and a shrine office. File:Suitengu shrine of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Water deity shrine File:Main approach to Unakorowake-jinja 2.JPG|Main approach File:Torii gate of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Torii === Subsidiary Shrines === The shrine precinct includes various stone shrines dedicated to deities such as {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mishima Taisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 三島神社}}, [[:en:Izusan Shrine|Izu-san Shrine]], [[:en:Hakone Shrine|Hakone Shrine]], and others. == Festivals == The Spring Festival is held annually from [[:en:April 2|April 2]], and the Autumn Festival occurs from [[:en:September 18|September 18]]. Historical records indicate that events such as horseback archery were once part of the celebrations. == Access == '''Address''' * [[:en:Fukushima Prefecture|Fukushima Prefecture]], [[:en:Kōriyama|Kōriyama]], Mihota-machi Hachiman, Kamino-dai 76 === Public Transportation === * From [[:en:Kōriyama Station|Koriyama Station]], take the No. 2 bus bound for Nagahama (approx. 35 minutes). [[:en:September 18|September 18]] (Autumn Festival) }} '''Unakorowake Shrine''' (宇奈己呂和気神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Kōriyama|Kōriyama]], [[:en:Fukushima Prefecture|Fukushima Prefecture]]. It is designated as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin Taisha|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}), with its former status being that of a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. == Enshrined Deities == '''Chief deity''' * '''{{ill|Seoritsu-hime|lt=Seoritsu-hime|lt=Seoritsu Hime|ja|瀬織津姫|1=Seoritsu-hime|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seoritsu Hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Seoritsu-hime|qq=}}''' – One of the {{ill|Haraedo no Kami|lt=Haraedo no Kami|lt=Haraedo no Ōkami|ja|祓戸大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haraedo no Ōkami|qq=}} deities '''Subsidiary Deities''' * Hachiman God: Homutawake-no-Mikoto ([[:en:Emperor Ōjin|Emperor Ōjin]]) == History == === Establishment === According to old records of the shrine, during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Kōnin|Emperor Kōnin]], the land of Mutsu Province was rife with disturbances caused by the Emishi. In the first year of Ten'ō (781), the imperial court dispatched {{ill|Fujiwara no Kuro Maro|ja|藤原小黒麻呂|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Kuro Maro|qq=|1=Fujiwara no Oguromaro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11623210}} as the Inspector of Mutsu and Dewa Provinces (陸奥出羽按察使), but this effort yielded no results. The following year, in June of the first year of Enryaku (782), the newly enthroned Emperor Kanmu appointed [[:en:Ōtomo no Yakamochi|Ōtomo no Yakamochi]] as Inspector of Mutsu and Dewa Provinces and Commander of the Defense Forces (鎮守府将軍) and sent him to the region. However, the Emishi's strength was formidable, and Yakamochi ascended {{ill|Takahatayama|ja|高旗山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takahatayama|qq=|1=Takahata Yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q31470237}} to perform purification rituals and offer prayers to the deities. In response, divine spirits manifested, and miraculous signs appeared on the mountains of Asaka and {{ill|Yatsuhatayama|ja|八ツ旗山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yatsuhatayama|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Emboldened by these divine signs, Yakamochi led a campaign to pacify the Emishi. Through his efforts, the rebellions in Mutsu and Dewa Provinces were subdued, and peace was restored to the land. In gratitude for the divine assistance, Yakamochi constructed a magnificent shrine on the summit of Takahatayama to enshrine the guardian deity. Over time, the shrine fell into disrepair, prompting its relocation to its current site in Yamazaki in the third year of Enryaku (784), where a new shrine building was constructed. The deity {{ill|Hachiman Ōkami|ja|八幡大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman Ōkami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八幡神|1=Hachiman|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q261637}} (Homuda Wake no Mikoto) was also enshrined as a secondary deity. At the entrance to the mountain trail (pilgrimage path) leading to Takahatayama, near {{ill|Genda Onsen|ja|郡山市内の温泉#源田温泉（forest バン源田）|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Genda Onsen|qq=|1=Genda Onsen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11643189}}, there is a signboard detailing this history, and the summit still houses a stone shrine (okumiya) dedicated to {{ill|Unakiorowake Shrine|ja|宇奈己呂和気神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Unakiorowake Shrine|qq=|1=Unakorowake Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17217367}}. According to the shrine’s traditions, it was established in the 11th year of Emperor Kinmei's reign (circa 550 CE) when the deity {{ill|Seoritsu-hime|lt=Seoritsu-hime|lt=Seoritsu Hime|ja|瀬織津比売|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seoritsu Hime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 瀬織津姫}} manifested on the summit of Takahatayama in Asaka District. In the shrine's records, Seoritsu Hime is identified as the same deity as {{ill|Yaso Magatsuhi no Mikoto|ja|八十禍津日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yaso Magatsuhi no Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, born from the impurities cleansed by [[:en:Izanagi|Izanagi]] during his purification ritual at {{ill|Awagihara|ja|阿波岐原|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Awagihara|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. Furthermore, Seoritsu Hime is associated with the "Ara-mitama" of Amaterasu Ōmikami, worshipped at the {{ill|Aramatsuri-no-Miya|ja|荒祭宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aramatsuri Shrine|qq=}} of [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Grand Shrine]] and [[:en:Hirota Shrine|Hirota Shrine]]. She is revered as a deity who purifies sins, impurities, and calamities in the world. This tradition reflects the prayers offered to Seoritsu Hime for the successful pacification of the Mutsu region, which had a fluctuating relationship with the Yamato court. The shrine is said to have been relocated from Takahatayama to its current location in the third year of Enryaku (784). === Historical Overview === According to the [[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Shoku Nihon Kōki]], in the 14th year of Shōwa (847), the deity of Unakiorowake Shrine was granted the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The [[:en:Ruijū Kokushi|Ruijū Kokushi]] records that in the 11th year of Jōgan (869), this Rank was elevated to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. Compiled in the 5th year of Enchō (927), the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]] designated Unakiorowake Shrine as a {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin Taisha|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, one of the major shrines of Asaka District’s three enshrined shrines. As the General Shrine (Sōsha) of the 33 Asaka villages, it commanded enduring respect and devotion from local leaders and residents. During the Kamakura period, [[:en:Kudō Suketsune|Kudō Suketsune]] was assigned as the local governor of Asaka District. He dispatched his son, {{ill|Asaka Suketaka|ja|安積祐長|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asaka Suketaka|qq=|1=Asaka no Suketaka|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q48761369}}, to manage the region. Recognizing the importance of “guardian worship” to secure public allegiance, Kudō Suketsune introduced deities from [[:en:Mishima Taisha|Mishima Taisha]], [[:en:Izusan Shrine|Izusan Shrine]], and [[:en:Hakone Shrine|Hakone Shrine]] into Asaka. Initially, these deities were enshrined as subsidiary gods of Unakiorowake Shrine rather than as principal deities, aiming to stabilize the populace and establish faith. Similar policies were adopted in the 6th year of Ōei (1399) when [[:en:Ashikaga Mitsukane|Ashikaga Mitsukane]] sent {{ill|Ashikaga Mitsunao|ja|足利満直|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashikaga Mitsunao|qq=|1=Ashikaga Mitsunao|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11636791}} and {{ill|Ashikaga Mitsusada|ja|足利満貞|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashikaga Mitsusada|qq=|1=Ashikaga Mitsusada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11636794}} to Mutsu and Dewa to solidify control. Upon arriving in Asaka District, Mitsunao sought to restore Unakiorowake Shrine. In the 9th year of Ōei (1402), he renovated the shrine buildings and grounds and appointed his retainer, Ōhara Yasunobu, as the shrine priest. The Ōhara family continues to serve as shrine priests to this day. After its relocation from Takahatayama, Hachiman Ōkami was enshrined as a secondary deity, leading to the shrine being known as “Hachiman Shrine” and later, during the Edo period, as “Aidan Hachiman Shrine.” Worship of the martial deity Hachiman Ōkami drew the reverence of local samurai. Historical records, including land donation documents granting 200 koku of land from lords such as Itō Taka-yuki, {{ill|Ashina Moritaka|ja|蘆名盛高|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashina Moritaka|qq=|1=Ashina Moritaka|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11625151}}, [[:en:Ashina Moriuji|Ashina Moriuji]], and [[:en:Gamō Ujisato|Gamo Ujisato]], as well as prayers from [[:en:Uesugi Kagekatsu|Uesugi Kagekatsu]] before the Battle of Sekigahara in Keichō 5 (1600), and the “Aidan Hachiman Documents,” have been preserved. In the 15th year of Meiji (1882), Unakiorowake Shrine was designated a village shrine (Gōsha). === Ranks === * Shōwa 14 (847): Elevated from no Rank to Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ([[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Shoku Nihon Kōki]]) * Jōgan 11 (869): Elevated from Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade, to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ([[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]) == Grounds == === Shrine buildings === The shrine complex includes the '''haiden''' (worship hall), '''heiden''' (offering hall), and the '''honden''' (main hall), which is a three-bay nagare-zukuri style structure with an enclosing roof. The '''honden''' features three doors, and according to shrine tradition, in addition to Seoritsu-hime and Hondawake-no-Mikoto, Kasuga Ōkami ({{ill|Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto|ja|天児屋根命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Koyane|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天児屋命}}) was once enshrined here. Currently, the shrine enshrines only Seoritsu-hime and Hondawake-no-Mikoto, leaving one seat vacant. File:Honden of Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|'''Honden'''
Three-bay nagare-zukuri style. File:Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|'''Haiden''' '''Interior of the Haiden''' The haiden displays large ema boards, including "Susanoo slaying Yamata-no-Orochi" and "Kato Kiyomasa hunting a tiger." Additionally, a plaque commemorates when [[:en:Itō Hirobumi|Itō Hirobumi]] visited the shrine during the Asaka Canal Completion tier 5]][[Category: ceremony and offered a heihaku fee of three yen. Other plaques, such as "Hachiman Shrine" and "Asaka Sōsha," are also displayed. File:Inside of Haiden of Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Interior of the haiden
The shrine mirror reveals the three doors of the honden. File:Inside of Haiden of Unakorowake-jinja 2.JPG|Plaques reading "Asaka Sōsha, Unakorowake Shrine" and "Hachiman Shrine." File:Inside of Haiden of Unakorowake-jinja 4.JPG|Plaque commemorating Itō Hirobumi’s donation: "Heihaku Fee: Three Yen, Councillor Itō Hirobumi." File:Ema board of "The story of Kiyomasa Kato hunting a tiger".JPG|Large ema: "Kato Kiyomasa hunting a tiger." File:Ema board of "The story of Susanowo slaying Yamata-no-Orochi".JPG|Large ema: "Susanoo slaying Yamata-no-Orochi." '''Other structures''' File:Kaguraden of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|'''Kaguraden''' (sacred dance stage) === Torii and approach === Passing through the '''torii''', visitors cross a small stream. To the west of the approach are a memorial stone and the '''Suitengū''' (dedicated to [[:en:Ame-no-Minakanushi|Ame-no-Minakanushi]]), while the shrine office lies to the right. File:Suitengu shrine of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Suitengū shrine within the grounds. File:Memorial stone of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Memorial stone along the approach. File:Main approach to Unakorowake-jinja 2.JPG|The shrine approach. File:Main approach to Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|The stone bridge and approach. File:Torii gate of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|The torii gate. == Auxiliary and subordinate shrines == To the west of the main shrine building lies the '''Yōsan Shrine''' (dedicated to Uka-no-Mitama-no-Kami and Wakumusubi-no-Kami) and a memorial shrine for the war dead. Additional stone shrines enshrine deities such as Mishima Shrine, Izusan Shrine, Hakone Shrine (all brought by Kudō Suketsune), Aosa Shrine, Yama Shrine, Inari Shrine, Kasuga Shrine, Tenman-gū, Itsukushima Shrine, and others. == Festivals == The spring grand festival takes place from April 2 to April 4, and the autumn grand festival occurs from September 18 to September 20. In the past, events such as yabusame (horseback archery) and mikoshi processions were held but were discontinued following the {{ill|Kakitsu Rebellion|ja|嘉吉の乱|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kakitsu Rebellion|qq=|1=Kakitsu Incident|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q5365139}} in 1441 and the [[:en:Kanshō famine|Great Famine of Chōroku and Kanshō]] in 1459. While attempts were made to revive the mikoshi processions under the protection of the Tanba clan during the Edo period, these rituals are no longer performed. == Access == '''location''' * 76 Kamino-dai, Hachiman, Mihota-machi, Kōriyama City, Fukushima Prefecture, Japan. === By bus === * From [[:en:Kōriyama Station (Fukushima)|Koriyama Station (Fukushima)]] (JR East Tōhoku Shinkansen), take the No. 2 bus bound for Naganuma (approx. 35 minutes) and alight at "Mihota Public Hall." The shrine is a short walk away. Check timetables for details. === By car === * About 10 minutes from {{ill|Kōriyama Minami Interchange (Fukushima)|ja|郡山南インターチェンジ (福島県)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōriyama Minami Interchange (Fukushima)|qq=|1=Koriyama-minami interchange|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11643156}}. == References == * ''Asaka no Jinja-shi'' (Fukushima Prefecture Shrine Office, Koriyama Branch, 2001), pp. 181–183, Unakorowake Shrine entry. * ''Zenkoku Jinja Meikan Vol. 1'' (National Shrine Directory Publishing Center, July 1977). == External links == {{Commonscat|Unakorowake-jinja}} * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/271001.html Unakorowake Shrine] (Kokugakuin University, 21st Century COE Program "Shinto and Shrine Archive"). {{Shinto}} {{Munakata Faith}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|宇奈己呂和気神社|version=85680187|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Koriyama]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Mutsu Province]] [[Category:Former Gō-sha in Fukushima Prefecture]] }} [[ja:宇奈己呂和気神社]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Koriyama]] {{Commons category|Unakorowake-jinja}} {{wikidata link|Q17217367}}

[[:en:September 18|September 18]] (Autumn Festival) | location = {{ill|Kōriyama|qid=Q264206}} }} '''Unakorowake Shrine''' (宇奈己呂和気神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Kōriyama|Kōriyama]], [[:en:Fukushima Prefecture|Fukushima Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinai shrine|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai shrine|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin taisha|qq=|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Myōjin Taisha|WD=Q9610964}}), and its former shrine Ranking under the [[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines]] was {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. [[Unakoro Waki Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == '''Main deity''' * '''{{ill|Seoritsu-hime|lt=Seoritsu-hime|lt=Seoritsuhime|ja|瀬織津比売命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seoritsuhime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' - One of the {{ill|Haraedo no Kami|lt=Haraedo no Kami|lt=Haraedo-no-Ōkami|ja|祓戸大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haraedo-no-Ōkami|qq=}} '''Secondary deity''' * [[:en:Hachiman|Hachiman]]: Hondawake-no-Mikoto ([[:en:Emperor Ōjin|Emperor Ōjin]]) == History == === Founding === According to ancient records, during the reign of [[:en:Emperor Kōnin|Emperor Kōnin]], disturbances caused by the [[:en:Emishi|Emishi]] were widespread in the Mutsu Province. In the first year of {{ill|Ten'ō|ja|天応 (日本)|1=Ten'ō|2=ja|3=天応 (日本)|qq=|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1373125}}{{citation needed|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten'ō|qq=}} ([[:en:781|781]]), the court dispatched {{ill|Fujiwara no Oguro|ja|藤原小黒麿|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Oguro|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} as inspector of Mutsu and Dewa, but he failed to suppress the unrest. The following year, in the first year of [[:en:Enryaku|Enryaku]] ([[:en:782|782]]), the newly enthroned [[:en:Emperor Kanmu|Emperor Kanmu]] sent [[:en:Ōtomo no Yakamochi|Ōtomo no Yakamochi]] to the region as an inspector and commander. After seeking divine guidance on {{ill|Takahatayama|ja|高旗山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takahatayama|qq=|1=Takahata Yama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q31470237}}, Yakamochi established a shrine to enshrine Seoritsuhime, whose divine power reportedly aided in subduing the unrest. Later, in the 3rd year of Enryaku ([[:en:784|784]]), the shrine was moved from Takahatayama to its current location in Yamazaki. At that time, {{ill|Hachiman|ja|八幡大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八幡神}} (Hondawake-no-Mikoto) was enshrined as a secondary deity. A stone shrine (okumiya) remains on the summit of Takahatayama, and an information board at the mountain trailhead near {{ill|Genda Onsen|ja|源田温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Genda Onsen|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} recounts this history. According to shrine records, the shrine’s origins trace back to the 11th year of Emperor Kinmei ([[:en:550|550]]?). During that time, Seoritsuhime was believed to have manifested on Takahatayama's summit. Seoritsuhime, identified as a deity born from the purification of {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊耶那岐命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} at Awagihara, was venerated for her ability to cleanse impurities and pacify disturbances. === Historical Overview === As recorded in the [[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Shoku Nihongi]], the shrine was granted the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 14th year of [[:en:Jōwa|Jōwa (Heian period)]] ([[:en:847|847]]). According to the [[:en:Ruijū Kokushi|Ruijū Kokushi]], the shrine's Rank was elevated to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in the 11th year of [[:en:Zhenguan|Jōgan]] ([[:en:869|869]]). In [[:en:927|927]], the shrine was listed as a {{ill|Myōjin taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin taisha|qq=|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Myōjin Taisha|WD=Q9610964}} in the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]] and became the main shrine of the three {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} in the Asaka District, receiving deep veneration from both rulers and local residents. It was also designated the total shrine (sōsha) for the {{ill|33 communities of Asaka|ja|安積三十三郷|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/33 communities of Asaka|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. During the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]], [[:en:Kudō Suketsune|Kudō Suketsune]], appointed as local governor, introduced deities from the [[:en:Mishima Taisha|Mishima Taisha]] and other shrines in Izu Province as subordinate shrines. The shrine was further restored by local rulers such as [[:en:Ashina clan (Japan)|Ashina clan]] and [[:en:Gamō Ujisato|Gamo Ujisato]], and it received land grants and other support. === typeings === * [[:en:Jōwa|Jōwa (Heian period)]] 14 ([[:en:847|847]]): Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ([[:en:Shoku Nihon Kōki|Shoku Nihongi]]) * [[:en:Zhenguan|Jōgan]] 11 ([[:en:869|869]]): Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ([[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]) == Shrine Grounds == === Main Shrine === The shrine comprises a haiden, heiden, and a covered three-bay honden in [[:en:Nagare-zukuri|Miya-zukuri]] style. The honden features three doors, symbolizing the deities enshrined. Presently, the shrine honors two deities, with one seat left vacant. File:Honden of Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Honden (Three-bay miya-zukuri style) File:Unakorowake-jinja 1.JPG|Haiden === Torii and Approach === A stream flows beneath the torii. The approach features memorial stones, subsidiary shrines, and a shrine office. File:Suitengu shrine of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Water deity shrine File:Main approach to Unakorowake-jinja 2.JPG|Main approach File:Torii gate of Unakorowake-jinja.JPG|Torii === Subsidiary Shrines === The shrine precinct includes various stone shrines dedicated to deities such as {{ill|Mishima Taisha|ja|三嶋神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mishima Taisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 三島神社}}, [[:en:Izusan Shrine|Izu-san Shrine]], [[:en:Hakone Shrine|Hakone Shrine]], and others. == Festivals == The Spring Festival is held annually from [[:en:April 2|April 2]], and the Autumn Festival occurs from [[:en:September 18|September 18]].
